Import each component from its own subpath (the `import` line on every export) to keep bundles small; the root `@punji/ui` re-exports everything.
Load styles once: `import '@punji/ui/styles.css'`, or per component from `@punji/ui/css/<name>.css` after `tokens.css` and `base.css`.

# Punji UI

> Accessible React components for money, markets and accounting: exact bigint amounts, NPR lakh and crore, Bikram Sambat dates and NEPSE tables. MIT, on npm.

- Package: @punji/ui 0.2.0 on npm (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@punji/ui), published from CI with provenance. MIT licence.
- Install: `npm install @punji/ui`. Peer dependencies: react@^19 and react-dom@^19. ESM only, TypeScript declarations included.
- Styles: import `@punji/ui/styles.css` once at the app root. Every module also has its own subpath (`@punji/ui/stock-table`) and stylesheet (`@punji/ui/css/stock-table.css`).
- Money is bigint minor units (paisa, cents) or exact decimal strings, never floating point; anything that divides takes an explicit rounding mode.
- Nepal first, any currency: NPR, lakh and crore grouping, Devanagari digits, Bikram Sambat (BS) dates, the Nepal fiscal year and the NEPSE session calendar are built in; other currencies and locales are configuration.
- Source: https://github.com/20was/punji-ui

Each link below is the page as Markdown (an index.md beside the HTML page): its text, props tables and example code.

- [Overview](https://design.punji.app/): every page, by domain

## Get started

- [Introduction and installation](https://design.punji.app/get-started/using/index.md): Install @punji/ui from npm, load the stylesheet once and render an exact NPR or USD amount in React. Who Punji UI is for, and how it differs from a generic kit.
- [Next.js App Router](https://design.punji.app/get-started/nextjs/index.md): Use @punji/ui in the Next.js App Router: import the CSS in the root layout, know which components are client components, and pass bigint safely.
- [Vite](https://design.punji.app/get-started/vite/index.md): Use @punji/ui in a Vite React and TypeScript app: create the project, import the stylesheet once in main.tsx and dedupe React when linking locally.
- [Using with a router](https://design.punji.app/get-started/router/index.md): Wrap your router link once with LinkProvider and every Punji link, button and row routes through it: React Router, Next.js Link and TanStack Router.
- [Theming and custom tokens](https://design.punji.app/get-started/theming/index.md): Every token is a --pu-* CSS variable in cascade layers. Switch theme, contrast and density, apply a bank brand with createTheme, and support RTL.
- [Server rendering and hydration](https://design.punji.app/get-started/ssr/index.md): Render Punji UI on the server and hydrate without warnings: hook-free components, useHydrated, useMediaQuery with a server value, and a pre-paint theme script.
- [Tailwind interop](https://design.punji.app/get-started/tailwind/index.md): Use Tailwind CSS v4 beside @punji/ui: declare the cascade layer order once so utilities win over Punji components and Tailwind preflight does not.
- [Live data adapters](https://design.punji.app/get-started/live-data/index.md): Feed live prices into Punji UI through an adapter and a hook, never from a fetch inside a component. Validate messages, keep bigint, tween with LiveFigure.
- [Security](https://design.punji.app/get-started/security/index.md): What the package does to stay safe (no HTML from strings, one dependency, signed releases) and what stays yours: formula injection, masking, server validation.
- [Localisation of component copy](https://design.punji.app/get-started/localisation/index.md): Translate Punji UI component copy with PunjiLocaleProvider and typed ne, hi and bn message packs, each its own import, with English fallback per key.
- [Roadmap](https://design.punji.app/get-started/roadmap/index.md): What ships today, what is in progress and what comes in waves 2 to 4: guides, compositions, portfolio components, scale, accessibility and example apps.
- [Contributing, for people and agents](https://design.punji.app/get-started/agents/index.md): Which Punji UI component to reach for, the checks to run before calling work done, and the bar a new component has to meet. For humans and coding agents.
- [Copy a pattern into your app](https://design.punji.app/get-started/copy-a-pattern/index.md): Copy a Punji UI Showcase screen into your React app with one shadcn CLI command: the TSX, its layout CSS and sample data, with @punji/ui as the dependency.

- [Wealth dashboard](https://design.punji.app/apps/wealth-dashboard/index.md): A personal wealth dashboard built from Punji UI: net worth, allocation, live holdings, dividends by fiscal year, an IPO centre with allotment, goals and CSV.
- [Accounting](https://design.punji.app/apps/accounting/index.md): A double-entry accounting app built from Punji UI: ledger, journals, trial balance, P&L and balance sheet by BS fiscal year, bank reconciliation, aging and TDS.
- [Billing and payroll](https://design.punji.app/apps/business/index.md): A billing and payroll app built from Punji UI: VAT invoices with PAN and amount in words, customers, payments, a payroll run with SSF and TDS, and payslips.
- [Retail banking](https://design.punji.app/apps/retail-banking/index.md): A mobile-first retail banking app built from Punji UI: balances, statements in BS and AD, a transfer with payee check and OTP, cards, loans, deposits and KYC.
- [Digital wallet](https://design.punji.app/apps/digital-wallet/index.md): An eSewa and Khalti class digital wallet built from Punji UI: balance and load money, scan and pay EMVCo QR, send to mobile with a PIN, bills, top-up, rewards.
- [Market portal](https://design.punji.app/apps/market-portal/index.md): A public NEPSE market portal built from Punji UI: indices, breadth, sector heatmap, a screener, a 10k-trade floorsheet, company pages, calendars and alerts.
- [Invest and insure](https://design.punji.app/apps/invest-insure/index.md): A mutual fund and insurance app built from Punji UI: fund explorer with riskometers, SIP planner and orders, portfolio XIRR, policies, claims and tax saving.

## Foundations

- [Colour tokens](https://design.punji.app/foundations/colour-tokens/index.md): Every colour is a --pu-color-* CSS variable in tokens.css. Light and dark follow the system, and data-theme forces one for any subtree.
- [Typography](https://design.punji.app/foundations/typography/index.md): Two font stacks, a fluid text scale and tabular figures so money columns align. Mukta is included, so Devanagari renders without a layout shift.
- [Spacing and shape](https://design.punji.app/foundations/spacing/index.md): A short space scale, a 32/36/44 control height scale and radii. Every control reads the one height scale, so toolbars line up.
- [Accessibility modes](https://design.punji.app/foundations/accessibility-modes/index.md): High-contrast themes at WCAG AAA, Windows forced colours, three densities with safe touch targets, and right-to-left layout. All are attributes.

## Financial primitives

- [MoneyDisplay](https://design.punji.app/components/money-display/index.md): Show one exact amount in any currency from bigint minor units, with tabular digits, locale-correct signs and a spoken currency name. React, accessible.
- [PriceChange](https://design.punji.app/components/price-change/index.md): Show the move between two prices as an amount and a percent. Direction is carried by sign, arrow shape and a spoken word, never by colour alone.
- [CurrencyInput](https://design.punji.app/components/currency-input/index.md): A React currency input for NPR, USD or any currency: groups digits as you type, accepts Devanagari digits and refuses extra decimals instead of rounding.
- [Financial calculations](https://design.punji.app/utilities/financial-calculations/index.md): Pure TypeScript for positions and ratios with no React or dependencies. Bigint ledger maths with a chosen rounding mode, plus display-only ratios.
- [Formatters](https://design.punji.app/utilities/formatters/index.md): Format money in JavaScript for any currency, plus Nepal helpers for lakh and crore grouping, Devanagari digits and BS dates. Exact inputs, no silent rounding.
- [Figure and Delta](https://design.punji.app/components/figure/index.md): Every number on a page: tabular digits with lakh and crore grouping, never truncated, and a change shown as a sign, an arrow, a colour and a spoken word.
- [Global money](https://design.punji.app/utilities/global-money/index.md): Exact money for any currency and locale: lakh/crore or western grouping, 0 to 3 decimals, 18 digit scripts, exact compact notation and ISO 4217 data.

## Stock market

- [Order book](https://design.punji.app/components/order-book/index.md): OrderBookDepth draws best bids and asks with depth bars and a buy/sell split; OrderBook is the plain table. Display only, no order placement.
- [CandlestickChart](https://design.punji.app/components/candlestick-chart/index.md): OHLC candlestick or bar chart with volume pane, moving averages, keyboard crosshair, gap-aware axes and a data table; aggregates large series, never drops them.
- [DepthChart](https://design.punji.app/components/depth-chart/index.md): Cumulative bid and ask depth from order book levels with mid price and spread, crossed and one-sided book handling, keyboard readout and a data table.
- [StockTable](https://design.punji.app/components/stock-table/index.md): A React stock table for NEPSE or any market: symbol, LTP, change, volume, turnover and a trend line. You own the data and sort; prices are exact bigint.
- [MarketMovers](https://design.punji.app/components/market-movers/index.md): Gainers, losers and most active as accessible tabs over one compact StockTable. rankMovers does the ranking, and an unchanged quote is never a mover.
- [MarketIndices](https://design.punji.app/components/market-indices/index.md): Index cards or a one-row strip showing value in points, change since the previous close and an optional trend line, with market status above.
- [MarketStatus and getMarketSession](https://design.punji.app/components/market-status/index.md): Show whether a market is open, pre-open, closed, halted or on holiday, as a word and a distinct icon, from a known state or getMarketSession.
- [PriceLimitIndicator](https://design.punji.app/components/price-limit/index.md): Show where the last traded price sits between the day's lower and upper circuit limits, with an at-limit flag. Exchange limits are the authority.
- [Watchlist](https://design.punji.app/components/watchlist/index.md): The stocks a person follows, in their own order, keyed by symbol so live prices change in place. Move and remove are real buttons you opt into.
- [MarketHeatmap](https://design.punji.app/components/market-heatmap/index.md): A squarified treemap where area is size and fill is change on a seven-step diverging scale. Deterministic layout; tiles print an arrow and signed change.
- [MarketBreadth](https://design.punji.app/components/market-breadth/index.md): Market breadth in React: advances, declines and unchanged as one split bar with counts, shares and the A/D ratio, plus circuit hits or 52-week highs.
- [PriceChart](https://design.punji.app/components/price-chart/index.md): A compact accessible line chart for a short labelled series. Missing values break the line instead of drawing zero, with a data table for every point.
- [Sparkline](https://design.punji.app/components/sparkline/index.md): A small trend line with no axes for use beside a printed figure. Missing values are dropped, never zero, and long series keep each bucket's extremes.
- [CompanySearch](https://design.punji.app/components/company-search/index.md): One field for symbol or name with ranked in-memory suggestions, as a finder or a picker, with a full-height sheet on phones. Nothing is fetched while typing.
- [LiveFigure](https://design.punji.app/components/live-figure/index.md): A figure fed by a live price: it counts to the new value over 450 ms and tints once in the direction of the change, and honours reduced motion.
- [NEPSE fees](https://design.punji.app/utilities/nepse-fees/index.md): Exact NEPSE trade costs in paisa: broker commission bands, SEBON fee, DP charge and capital gains tax by holding period, all configurable.
- [OrderTicket](https://design.punji.app/components/order-ticket/index.md): A buy or sell ticket for NEPSE: lot and tick steps, tick snapping, a circuit band check and an exact fee estimate before a confirm step.
- [OrderList and TradeList](https://design.punji.app/components/order-list/index.md): A trader's order book and trade book: status in words, filled share, Modify and Cancel with a confirm, and announced status changes.
- [TradingHaltBanner](https://design.punji.app/components/trading-halt/index.md): A banner for an index circuit breaker, an exchange halt or resumed trading, announced at once, with the move and the resume time in words.

- [PortfolioAllocation](https://design.punji.app/components/portfolio-allocation/index.md): Where the money sits, by holding or sector, as a donut or bar with a legend. Small slices gather into Other and the shares always add up to exactly 100.
- [PortfolioOverview](https://design.punji.app/components/portfolio-overview/index.md): A portfolio's headline: value, day change, invested amount, unrealised and realised P&L and return on cost, with loading and error states.
- [DividendHistory](https://design.punji.app/components/dividend-history/index.md): Dividends, bonus shares and rights by Nepal fiscal year (BS labels) as a stacked column chart and an exact table, with cash yield where a value is given.
- [TransactionHistory](https://design.punji.app/components/transaction-history/index.md): Buys, sells, bonus, rights and dividends as a filterable, paged list. Each sale shows its realised P&L from computePosition; filters never change it.

- [MeterBar and RangeBar](https://design.punji.app/components/meter-range/index.md): MeterBar lays parts on one track with a benchmark marker; RangeBar shows where a value sits among others. Decorative unless labelled; print figures beside them.
- [HeadlineFigure and FigureChip](https://design.punji.app/components/headline-figure/index.md): A page's lead figure: a quiet label, the figure large, and changes as FigureChips. The figure never truncates and chip tint never carries direction.
- [KeyStats and FactList](https://design.punji.app/components/key-stats/index.md): KeyStats lays a panel's facts as label-over-value cells; FactList is one column of label-and-value lines. Unknown values say so in words, never zero.
- [SplitBar, DivergingBar and NetBar](https://design.punji.app/components/split-bars/index.md): SplitBar, DivergingBar and NetBar print beside their figures: parts of a whole, rises and falls from a centre line, and a signed net with its parts.
- [RiskMeter](https://design.punji.app/components/risk-meter/index.md): A mutual fund riskometer in React: six levels from Low to Very high as a half-dial or a compact row of steps, with the level always printed in words.
- [Invest helpers](https://design.punji.app/utilities/invest-helpers/index.md): Pure exact mutual fund maths: XIRR by bisection on bigint fixed point, SIP and step-up projections, the SIP for a goal, units at a NAV and life cover needed.

- [JournalEntryView](https://design.punji.app/components/journal-entry/index.md): One journal with its lines, totals row and status. An unbalanced entry says 'Out of balance by' with a warning icon, never by colour alone.

- [StatementTable](https://design.punji.app/components/statement-table/index.md): An income statement, balance sheet or cash-flow style report from a typed tree of lines, one column per period, with optional change columns.
- [PaymentStatus](https://design.punji.app/components/payment-status/index.md): Show where an invoice or bill stands: paid, partly paid, unpaid, overdue or void, as a pill with its own icon and words. It labels, never decides.
- [FinancialPeriodSelector](https://design.punji.app/components/period-selector/index.md): Pick a reporting period from a list you supply, with a choice of period kind that keeps the time span. Nepal builders make fiscal years, quarters and months.
- [Ledger helpers](https://design.punji.app/utilities/ledger-helpers/index.md): Pure bigint maths for bookkeeping screens: journal totals and balance checks, running balances, trial balance, statement roll-ups and an exact ledgerToCsv.
- [Rows and lists](https://design.punji.app/components/rows/index.md): A grouped card of rows: ValueRow with a tile, title, line, figure and note as a link, a button or plain, and DataRows for label and value facts.

- [TaxInvoice](https://design.punji.app/components/tax-invoice/index.md): A printable Nepal VAT invoice: seller and buyer PAN, invoice number, BS and AD dates, lines, discount, exact 13% VAT, total and amount in words.
- [LineItemEditor](https://design.punji.app/components/line-item-editor/index.md): Editable bill lines with exact totals: description, quantity, rate and VAT per line; subtotal, taxable, VAT and total update as you type, in bigint paisa.
- [IncomeTaxCalculator](https://design.punji.app/components/income-tax-calculator/index.md): An income tax estimate from slabs you pass as data: single or couple, SSF, CIT and PF contributions with caps, rebates, and a band-by-band table.
- [Payslip](https://design.punji.app/components/payslip/index.md): A printable payslip: employer and employee with PAN, earnings and deductions side by side, gross, deductions and net pay in figures and words.
- [AgingTable](https://design.punji.app/components/aging-table/index.md): Receivables or payables aging by party: not due, 0–30, 31–60, 61–90 and over 90 days, with exact row and column totals and each bucket's share.
- [TdsSummary](https://design.punji.app/components/tds-summary/index.md): Tax deducted at source by category or entry: rate, payments, gross paid and TDS withheld with exact totals, plus formula-safe CSV for returns.
- [ReconciliationMatcher](https://design.punji.app/components/reconciliation-matcher/index.md): Bank reconciliation in React: match statement lines to ledger entries one-to-one or many-to-one, accept exact suggestions, and see the reconciliation statement.

## Trust and safety

- [DematAccountCard](https://design.punji.app/components/demat-account-card/index.md): A demat account as a card: holder, BOID split into DP ID and client ID, DP, CRN, masked bank account, status and renewal dates with warnings.
- [CorporateActionTimeline](https://design.punji.app/components/corporate-action-timeline/index.md): Book close, AGM, right issue and listing dates in order, in BS and AD, marked done, today or upcoming in words, with the next date highlighted.
- [EdisConfirmation](https://design.punji.app/components/edis-confirmation/index.md): Confirm an EDIS transfer of sold shares to the broker: pick the sales, see the exact unit total, accept the declaration and enter the PIN.
- [Share issue helpers](https://design.punji.app/utilities/share-issue-helpers/index.md): Pure helpers: issue status, kitta rules, BOID checks, bonus and right entitlements, adjusted price after book close and WACC, exact in bigint.

## Data

- [DataTable and FinancialTable](https://design.punji.app/components/data-table/index.md): A React financial table: typed rows, render callbacks, a sticky header, controlled sorting, and loading, error and empty states, built on DataTable.
- [VirtualFinancialTable and TableExport](https://design.punji.app/components/virtual-table/index.md): Virtualised table for 10,000+ financial rows with pinned and resizable columns, multi-column sort, live updates and formula-safe CSV export.
- [ColumnChart](https://design.punji.app/components/column-chart/index.md): Stacked columns per period with totals printed over each column and a labelled scale that includes zero. Never smoothed or 3D; gaps are never zero.
- [Chart math](https://design.punji.app/utilities/chart-math/index.md): Pure chart maths: nice ticks, band and time scales, OHLC validation, weekly or monthly candles, downsampling, SMA, EMA, rebasing and order book depth.
- [CSV export](https://design.punji.app/utilities/csv-export/index.md): toCsv writes RFC 4180 CSV from typed rows, and downloadText saves it. Cells starting with =, +, -, @ are neutralised so spreadsheets do not run them.
- [ShowMore](https://design.punji.app/components/show-more/index.md): The last line of a long list inside its card, "Show all 24" and "Show fewer": a full-width quiet button that says whether the list is open.
- [Avatar](https://design.punji.app/components/avatar/index.md): A person's initials in a circle for an account line, a list row or the account button: from the name or email, never a photo, with a skeleton while loading.
- [StatGrid and StatTile](https://design.punji.app/components/stat-grid/index.md): Figures two by two, four across on a wide screen: a quiet label, the figure and a note, as a description list so a screen reader pairs each term with its value.
- [Chart scales](https://design.punji.app/utilities/chart-scale/index.md): Pure Y scales for value charts: round ticks that bracket the line so it fills the plot, and a far-off second series named instead of squashed at the edge.

## Forms

- [DatePicker](https://design.punji.app/components/date-picker/index.md): A Nepali date picker for React: Bikram Sambat (BS) and Gregorian (AD) calendars, Nepali or English labels, strict typed input, bounds and keyboard support.
- [Button](https://design.punji.app/components/button/index.md): Primary, secondary, ghost and danger buttons in three sizes, icon-only with a required accessible name, a loading state, and link rendering with href.
- [NepalAddressPicker](https://design.punji.app/components/nepal-address-picker/index.md): Province, district, local level and ward for Nepali KYC forms, with all 753 local levels loaded on demand from their own subpath.
- [IdNumberInput](https://design.punji.app/components/id-number-input/index.md): KYC field for a Nepali PAN or citizenship certificate number: Devanagari digits accepted, letters refused, a clear shape message on leaving the field.
- [DocumentUpload](https://design.punji.app/components/document-upload/index.md): KYC documents step: one slot per document with its own types, size limit and camera, image preview, remove, and clear rejection messages.
- [OnboardingWizard](https://design.punji.app/components/onboarding-wizard/index.md): Multi-step onboarding shell: progress steps, current step heading, Back and Continue in a real form, focus moved and announced on each step change.
- [KYC helpers](https://design.punji.app/utilities/kyc-helpers/index.md): Shape checks for a Nepali PAN and citizenship certificate number, with Devanagari digits accepted. Typing-slip checks, not verification.
- [Field](https://design.punji.app/components/field/index.md): Text, number, price, date, symbol, select and long-text fields: a label over a boxed input with a hint or an error, correctly wired for screen readers.
- [Select](https://design.punji.app/components/select/index.md): The one dropdown: a real native select in the kit box, with grouped options, loading and disabled states and a themed picker where the browser supports it.
- [SegmentedControl](https://design.punji.app/components/segmented-control/index.md): A small set of exclusive options in one track: periods, windows, scopes. A toggle group by default, or ARIA tabs when it controls a panel.
- [Checkbox](https://design.punji.app/components/checkbox/index.md): One of several choices that can each be on, or a yes or no that waits for Save: a real checkbox in its label, with a lead swatch and an end count.
- [Switch](https://design.punji.app/components/switch/index.md): An on or off setting that takes effect at once: a button with role switch and aria-checked, named by the row's title, with a busy state while it saves.
- [RangeSlider](https://design.punji.app/components/range-slider/index.md): One track, two thumbs: a minimum and a maximum, each a native range input with its own keyboard and a spoken value, for filters like yield or price.
- [ChoiceGroup](https://design.punji.app/components/choice-group/index.md): Exclusive filters as native radio buttons with an underline or a compact look, so the browser provides arrow keys, one tab stop and disabled handling.
- [ListFilter](https://design.punji.app/components/list-filter/index.md): A list's own search field over rows already on the page, matched in memory: an x button and Esc clear it, and an optional slash key focuses it.
- [Chip and ChipRow](https://design.punji.app/components/chip/index.md): A pill you press to filter or toggle, and a single-choice row of them: sector filters, quick amounts and section jumps, with counts and a 44px tap area.
- [FilterChip](https://design.punji.app/components/filter-chip/index.md): One filter that is set, in words ("P/B 0.00 to 1.20"): press to edit it, press the x to remove it, with a caret for lists and a ring for an error.
- [PercentageInput](https://design.punji.app/components/percentage-input/index.md): A field for rates such as brokerage, commission and interest. The value is an exact decimal string, never a float, with Devanagari digits and min and max.
- [OtpInput](https://design.punji.app/components/otp-input/index.md): A one-time code field with one box per character: paste and SMS autofill, numeric or alphanumeric, masked option, one group label, and left-to-right in RTL.
- [StatementUpload](https://design.punji.app/components/statement-upload/index.md): Choose or drop a CSV or PDF statement. Checks type, size, empty files and duplicates with clear messages, shows name and size, and never makes a request.
- [Date range presets](https://design.punji.app/utilities/date-range-presets/index.md): Quick ranges for DateRangePicker: Today, This week, This month, Last 30 days and the Nepal fiscal year (Shrawan to Asar) to date, as pure exact functions.
- [PanInput](https://design.punji.app/components/pan-input/index.md): A field for a Nepal PAN or VAT number: nine digits, Devanagari accepted, spaces and hyphens dropped, with a clear message once the field is left.

## Layout

- [Card](https://design.punji.app/components/card/index.md): One surface for one section of a page: an optional header with title, line, count and one action, then content. Rows use hairlines, never nested cards.
- [CardLink](https://design.punji.app/components/card-link/index.md): The one text link in a card's header: in-app paths stay in the tab with a chevron, external addresses open a new tab with the new-tab words spoken.
- [LinkTable and StockLabel](https://design.punji.app/components/link-table/index.md): A short list where every row opens something, with quiet column heads and right-aligned figures that never truncate. Compact layout under 560px.
- [Pagination](https://design.punji.app/components/pagination/index.md): Page through a list: '6-10 of 12', numbered pages and named previous/next icon buttons. Takes the usePagination hook's state directly.
- [Tabs](https://design.punji.app/components/tabs/index.md): The views of one section as ARIA tabs with an underline on the chosen one, plus PanelTabs for a side panel: an icon over a short label.
- [Popover](https://design.punji.app/components/popover/index.md): A panel anchored under the control that opened it: Esc and a click outside close it, focus moves in and returns, and a portal mode avoids clipping.
- [Drawer](https://design.punji.app/components/drawer/index.md): A modal side panel that slides in from the right for a form over the page: Tab stays inside, Esc and the scrim close it, and focus returns to the opener.
- [CommandPalette](https://design.punji.app/components/command-palette/index.md): The command-K dialog: a search field over grouped results run by keyboard, with entity rows that carry action chips and spoken, announced choices.
- [Page layout and header](https://design.punji.app/components/page-layout/index.md): The page ground, the page header with a back circle, a large title, a meta line and up to three actions, and the section header: a title with one action.
- [AppShell](https://design.punji.app/components/app-shell/index.md): Router-independent page landmarks: a skip link, a header with brand and actions, a navigation, the main area and a footer. Navigation wraps on phones.
- [Sheet and Dock](https://design.punji.app/components/sheet/index.md): A short modal decision for one or two controls, with Tab trapped and Esc to close, and a sticky Dock that keeps the page's main action in reach at the bottom.
- [DrawerScreen](https://design.punji.app/components/drawer-screen/index.md): The inside of a Drawer: a screen with a header (title, back, close), a body and a footer that keeps Save and Cancel in reach however long the form is.
- [Stack and Cluster](https://design.punji.app/components/stack/index.md): Two layout primitives: Stack puts children in one column and Cluster in a row that wraps, both spaced by the --pu-space-* scale and nothing else.
- [CodeBlock](https://design.punji.app/components/code-block/index.md): A monospace box for plain text people read or copy, such as a CSV export or a JSON payload, with an optional label and Copy button. No syntax highlighting.
- [SplitPane](https://design.punji.app/components/split-pane/index.md): Two panes with a separator you drag or move with the keyboard: a WAI-ARIA window splitter that stacks the panes in a narrow container.

## Feedback

- [InlineState](https://design.punji.app/components/inline-state/index.md): A state shown inside a card where its data would be: locked, failed, empty, offline, stale or slow, with an icon tile, one line and its actions.
- [RetryNote](https://design.punji.app/components/retry-note/index.md): A part of a page failed to load: say so in its own place with a Try again button while the rest stays. An alert that screen readers announce.
- [EmptyState, Note and Skeleton](https://design.punji.app/components/empty-skeleton/index.md): EmptyState covers empty and error states, Note qualifies nearby data, and Skeleton holds the space of loading content so nothing jumps.
- [CheckList, CheckRow and StatusDisc](https://design.punji.app/components/check-list/index.md): A list of checks with an icon disc, title, one line, figure, status in words and chevron. Rows can be buttons, links, plain, or a vertical tab list.
- [StepList](https://design.punji.app/components/step-list/index.md): What to do first as numbered steps, each a title and one line, with the current step marked aria-current. Tiles, rows or a dismissible first-visit banner.
- [Toast](https://design.punji.app/components/toast/index.md): What just happened: saved, failed or info messages in a polite live region, with an optional undo, wrapped once in ToastProvider and raised with useToast.
- [Tooltip and InfoTip](https://design.punji.app/components/tooltip/index.md): A control's name on hover and focus, and a visible info button that explains a label. Neither holds the only copy of a fact, because a phone has no hover.
- [StatusPill](https://design.punji.app/components/status-pill/index.md): A short label for a state, a tone or a tag such as Bonus or New, with a marker form beside a title, and a CountBadge for how many are waiting.
- [LockedNote](https://design.punji.app/components/locked-note/index.md): The locked state of a data view: a lock and a plain line saying what is not included on this account. Never a plan name, never a blurred fake of the data.
- [InlineConfirm](https://design.punji.app/components/inline-confirm/index.md): The second step of a destructive action, in place of the row that asked: a question, a danger button that names what goes, and the way back, with Esc to cancel.
- [StatusTag](https://design.punji.app/components/status-tag/index.md): The state of a setting at the end of its row in a word or two, such as View only, On or Off: quiet, read and never pressed, with an optional small icon.

guides.money-rules:
# Conventions - Money is integer minor units as bigint (12550n is 125.50 in a 2-decimal currency); never pass money through Number. - Import each component from its own subpath (the `import` line on every export) to keep bundles small; the root `@punji/ui` re-exports everything. - Load styles once: `import '@punji/ui/styles.css'`, or per component from `@punji/ui/css/.css` after `tokens.css` and `base.css`. - Interactive components are client components (`use client`); pure helpers run anywhere, including on the server. - Labels are English by default; every component takes `labels` (or props) for other languages. Pass `money` or a formatter config for locale and digits. - Display components never move money: re-check amounts, payees and limits on your server. --- # Money rules Amounts are `bigint` minor units (paisa, cents) or exact decimal strings. Never pass a JavaScript `number` or a float to a money prop, never round-trip money through `Number`, `parseFloat` or `toFixed`. Anything that divides takes an explicit rounding mode. `JSON.stringify` cannot serialise a `bigint`: send minor units as decimal strings and call `BigInt()` on the client. ```tsx // 125.50 in a 2-decimal currency // exact decimal string is fine // wrong: a float ``` --- # Global money and locales The money formatter (`@punji/ui/money`) is currency-generic and exact: amounts are bigint minor units, the integer and fraction are split with bigint, and only the sign, symbol and spacing come from Intl. This page covers what goes beyond NPR: grouping, minor units, digit scripts, compact notation, ISO 4217 data and amounts in words. ## Grouping: lakh/crore or thousands Grouping follows the locale (CLDR): `en-IN`, `hi`, `ne`, `bn-BD` and `ta-LK` print `12,34,567`; `en-US`, `en-PK`, `en-LK` and `ar` print `1,234,567`. `MoneyFormatter#southAsian` is read from what Intl actually prints. Local practice does not always match CLDR. Many Pakistani screens group in lakh and crore although CLDR's `en-PK` does not, so `grouping` overrides the locale: ```ts createMoneyFormatter({ currency: 'PKR', locale: 'en-PK', grouping: 'south-asian', exponent: 2 }).format(123456789n); // 'Rs 12,34,567.89' createMoneyFormatter({ currency: 'INR', locale: 'en-IN', grouping: 'western' }).format(123456789n); // '₹1,234,567.89' ``` `grouping: 'south-asian'` also switches `formatCompact` to L / Cr / Arba / Kharba, and `parse` accepts the same grouping back. ## Minor units: 0, 2, 3 (and 4) The exponent comes from Intl: JPY 0, USD 2, KWD/BHD/OMR/JOD/TND/LYD 3. Where your ledger follows ISO 4217 and CLDR prints fewer decimals because the coins are out of use (AFN, ALL, COP, HUF, IDR, IQD, IRR, KPW, LAK, LBP, MGA, MMK, PKR, RSD, SOS, SYP, YER), pass `exponent`: ```ts import { isoMinorUnits } from '@punji/ui/money/iso4217'; createMoneyFormatter({ currency: 'IQD', locale: 'en', exponent: isoMinorUnits('IQD') }).format(1234567n); // 'IQD 1,234.567' ``` ## Digits of 18 scripts Input (`parse`, `toCanonicalInput`, `parseLocalizedDecimal`, `parseNumber`, every money and number field) accepts the decimal digits of `DIGIT_SCRIPTS`: Latin, Devanagari, Bengali, Arabic-Indic, Extended Arabic-Indic (Persian, Urdu), Thai, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Tibetan and full-width. Output follows the locale or `numberingSystem`: ```ts createMoneyFormatter({ currency: 'BDT', locale: 'bn-BD' }).format(123456789n); // '১২,৩৪,৫৬৭.৮৯৳' createMoneyFormatter({ currency: 'THB', locale: 'th-TH', numberingSystem: 'thai' }).format(123456789n); // '฿๑,๒๓๔,๕๖๗.๘๙' createMoneyFormatter({ currency: 'KWD', locale: 'ar-KW' }).format(123456789n); // Arabic-Indic digits, 3 decimals toAsciiDigits('١٢٣ ১২৩ ๑๒๓'); // '123 123 123' toScriptDigits('2026', 'beng'); // '২০২৬' ``` A test checks each digit set against Intl's own output for that numbering system. ## Compact notation, rounded once `formatCompact` is display-rounded, but it rounds once, from the exact amount. South Asian grouping uses bigint half-up rounding into L / Cr / Arba / Kharba (99.999 lakh becomes 1 Cr, not 100 L). Other locales pass the exact decimal string to Intl's compact notation, which rounds the decimal itself, so no binary float is involved: ```ts const usd = createMoneyFormatter({ currency: 'USD', locale: 'en' }); usd.formatCompact(99999999n); // '$1M' (999,999.99) usd.formatCompact(99999499n); // '$999.99K' usd.formatCompact(123456789012345678901n); // '$1,234,567.89T' (beyond 2^53, still exact) ``` Never store or sum a compact figure. ## ISO 4217 data, loaded on demand `@punji/ui/money/iso4217` (about 1.4 kB gzip) has the active currencies (List One, amendments through 2026: ZWG, XCG, SLE in; HRK, BGN, ZWL, ANG, SLL out) with numeric codes and ISO minor units. Funds, metals and test codes are left out. Names come from `Intl.DisplayNames` in the reader's language. ```ts const { getIso4217, getIso4217ByNumeric, currencyName } = await import('@punji/ui/money/iso4217'); getIso4217('npr'); // { code: 'NPR', numeric: '524', minorUnits: 2 } getIso4217ByNumeric(414); // KWD currencyName('NPR', 'ne'); // 'नेपाली रूपैयाँ' ``` ## Amounts in words for any currency `integerInWords` and `amountInWords` take `system: 'international'` (thousand, million, billion, trillion) beside the default South Asian system, and `fractionAsDigits` for the cheque style "and 50/100". `currencyAmountInWords` names the units: ```ts currencyAmountInWords(125050n, 'USD'); // 'One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars and Fifty Cents Only' currencyAmountInWords(1234567n, 'KWD'); // '... Dinars and Five Hundred Sixty-Seven Fils Only' currencyAmountInWords(1050n, 'BRL'); // 'Ten Brazilian Reals and 50/100 Only' ``` NPR, INR, PKR, LKR and BDT read in lakh and crore; currencies without built-in unit words use Intl's English plural name and a "50/100" fraction. English only; for other languages pass `numberWords` and `scaleWords`, or your own text. ## The Money value and which formatter to use `money(minor, 'USD')` returns `{ minor: bigint, currency }`. `isSameCurrency`, `addMoney` and `subtractMoney` never mix currencies silently: mixed input throws a `TypeError`. `Figure` and `Delta` take a `Money` as `value` (and an optional `formatter`) and print it through `createMoneyFormatter`; plain numbers stay for percent, ratio and count. `kind="rs"` and `compactRs` are deprecated in favour of `formatter.formatCompact`. Chart price props (`formatPrice`, `formatValue`, `format`) default to en-IN NPR; pass a formatter-backed function for another currency. --- # MoneyDisplay > Show one exact amount in any currency from bigint minor units, with tabular digits, locale-correct signs and a spoken currency name. React, accessible. URL: https://design.punji.app/components/money-display/ Section: Financial primitives (components) One exact amount in any currency. The amount is a bigint of minor units (or an exact decimal string); digits are tabular; sign, symbol and spacing follow the locale; a screen reader hears the full currency name when a symbol is shared. A missing value is a dash with a spoken "No value", never zero. ## When to use - Any money a reader sees: balances, prices, fees, totals. - With `nepalMoneyConfig`() for lakh and crore grouping. - compact for tight spaces, knowing it is display-rounded. ## When not to use - Formatting a number that is not money: use Figure or `formatNepalNumber`. - Showing the result of a calculation: compute with @punji/ui/calculations, then display the bigint it returns. - Passing a floating-point number: it would lose exactness, so the type does not allow it. ## API ### MoneyDisplay (component, from @punji/ui/money-display) | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | value (required) | `string \| bigint \| null \| undefined` | | Integer minor units (paisa, cents), or an exact decimal string in major units ('1234.50'). null/undefined show the missing mark. | | compact | `boolean \| MoneyCompactOptions` | | Shorten for tight spaces (lakh/crore or K/M/B). Display-rounded: the exact amount stays in the spoken text and the data value. | | missing | `string` | | Printed for a missing value. Default '—'. | | missingLabel | `string` | | Spoken for a missing value. Default 'No value'. | | className | `string` | | Extra class added to the outer element. | | testId | `string` | | Test id on the outer element. | | ref | `Ref` | | Ref to the outer element. | | locale | `string` | | BCP 47 tag; decides separators, symbol placement and digits. Default 'en'. | | display | `CurrencyDisplay` | | How the currency prints. 'none' prints the number only. Default 'symbol'. | | accounting | `boolean` | | Negative amounts in parentheses where the locale has an accounting style. Default false. | | signDisplay | `MoneySignDisplay` | | When to print the sign: 'auto' (default), 'always', 'exceptZero', 'negative' or 'never'. | | numberingSystem | `string` | | Intl numbering system, for example 'deva' for Devanagari digits. Default: the locale's. | | grouping | `MoneyGrouping` | | Override the locale's digit grouping. 'south-asian' also switches compact notation to lakh/crore. Default 'locale'. | | exponent | `number` | | Minor-unit digits, 0–9, when they differ from Intl's (ISO 4217 says IQD 3 where CLDR says 0). Default: `currencyExponent(currency)`. | | currency | `string` | | ISO 4217 code ('NPR', 'USD', 'JPY'). Sets the symbol and the number of minor-unit digits. | | preset | `MoneyFormatConfig` | | Base configuration, for example `nepalMoneyConfig()`. Other props override it. | ### MoneyFormatConfig (type, from @punji/ui/money) | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | currency (required) | `string` | | ISO 4217 code, for example 'USD', 'JPY', 'NPR'. | | locale | `string` | | BCP 47 tag; decides separators, symbol placement and digits. Existing `1` to `4` and `16` are unchanged. - **Type**: weights `regular/medium/semibold/bold` (400/500/600/700), line heights `tight` 1.2 and `normal` 1.5. `--pu-font-numeric` is the `font-variant-numeric` for figures; override it to `normal` to turn tabular figures off everywhere. - `scripts/check-css.mjs` (part of `npm run lint`) fails if a scale is not strictly increasing or a `var(--pu-*)` has no definition. **Deprecated** (still defined with their original, non-monotonic values; components no longer read them; removed in the next major): | Deprecated | Value | Use instead | | --- | --- | --- | | `--pu-radius-sm` | `0.5rem` | `--pu-radius-8` | | `--pu-radius-md` | `16px` | `--pu-radius-16` | | `--pu-radius-lg` | `16px` | `--pu-radius-16` | | `--pu-radius-xl` | `8px` | `--pu-radius-8` | | `--pu-radius-2xl` | `8px` | `--pu-radius-8` | | `--pu-radius-3xl` | `8px` | `--pu-radius-8` | Note: overriding a deprecated name no longer restyles components. Override the scale step or the card and control aliases. ## Stacking (z-index) Components read one scale, so layers never collide. Low to high, with gaps for your own layers in between. A popover or tooltip opened inside a drawer or sheet sits above it, and toasts sit above modals. | Token | Value | Used by | | --- | --- | --- | | `--pu-z-base` | `0` | page content | | `--pu-z-raised` | `1` | a lifted element inside one component | | `--pu-z-sticky` | `100` | dock, drawer header and footer | | `--pu-z-dropdown` | `200` | option lists, suggestions | | `--pu-z-overlay` | `1000` | drawer, sheet and command palette backdrops | | `--pu-z-modal` | `1100` | full-screen company search sheet | | `--pu-z-popover` | `1200` | popovers, including their full-screen form on phones | | `--pu-z-toast` | `1300` | toasts | | `--pu-z-tooltip` | `1400` | tooltips | | `--pu-z-skip-link` | `1500` | skip links | ## Reduced motion With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, every element whose class starts with `kit-` or `pu-` (and its `::before` and `::after`) gets near-instant animations and transitions, from the `punji.components` layer. The loading spinner keeps turning, and progress that JS drives (the hold-to-confirm fill) still updates. ## Density and direction Set on `:root` and by `data-pu-density` (control heights included); `--pu-dir` follows `dir`. Full table and touch-target rules: [THEMING.md](THEMING.md#density). | Token | Default (comfortable) | compact | spacious | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `--pu-cell-x` | `12px` | `8px` | `16px` | | `--pu-cell-y` | `10px` | `5px` | `14px` | | `--pu-control-lg` | `44px` | `36px` (`44px` on coarse pointers) | `52px` | | `--pu-control-md` | `36px` | `32px` (`36px` on coarse pointers) | `44px` | | `--pu-control-sm` | `32px` | `28px` | `36px` | | `--pu-row-lg` | `72px` | `56px` | `80px` | | `--pu-row-min` | `48px` | `36px` | `56px` | | `--pu-dir` | `1` | `-1` under `dir="rtl"` | - | ## Gain and loss colour convention `--pu-color-gain` and `--pu-color-loss` are what a rise and a fall look like; components read only these. The theme sets them (`createTheme({ finance: 'red-up' })` swaps them). The fixed hues `--pu-hue-green`, `--pu-hue-green-soft`, `--pu-hue-red` and `--pu-hue-red-soft` do not swap: they are what a component's `convention` prop points gain and loss at (`[data-convention='red-up']` or `'green-up']`). `createTheme` writes `--pu-finance-convention` (absent means `green-up`). In the light theme gain (`#284800`) and loss (`#a3321f`) differ in lightness by 1.50:1 as well as hue; the contrast gate requires 1.4:1 in every theme. See [THEMING.md](THEMING.md#gain-and-loss-colour-convention). --- # Colour tokens > Every colour is a --pu-color-* CSS variable in tokens.css. Light and dark follow the system, and data-theme forces one for any subtree. URL: https://design.punji.app/foundations/colour-tokens/ Section: Foundations (foundations) Every colour is a --pu-color-* CSS variable defined in @punji/ui/tokens.css. Light and dark follow the system; data-theme="light" or "dark" on any element forces one for that subtree. Components read tokens, never literals, so overriding a token moves everything built on it. ## When to use - Read tokens in your own CSS with var(`--pu-color-text`) so your screens follow the theme. - Override a token on a wrapper to re-theme one subtree. ## When not to use - Copying hex values into your CSS: they will not follow dark mode. - Using colour alone to show gain or loss: the sign and words must carry it. ## Example: Swatches Read from the shipped tokens.css at build time. {group.title}

{group.names .map((short) => `--pu-color-${short}`) .filter((name) => light.has(name)) .map((name) => { const l = light.get(name)!; const d = dark.get(name) ?? l; return ( {name} {l} · {d} ); })}
))} ); } ``` ## Example: Override a subtree data-theme on a wrapper forces one theme for everything inside it. ```tsx import { MoneyDisplay } from '@punji/ui/money-display'; import { PriceChange } from '@punji/ui/price-change'; const Panel = ({ theme }: { theme: 'light' | 'dark' }) => (

data-theme="{theme}"

); } ``` ## Keyboard behaviour - Tokens are not interactive. ## Accessibility - Text tokens are checked for contrast against their surfaces in both themes by the package visual gate. - Gain and loss tokens are always paired with a sign or word in components. ## Responsive behaviour - Tokens do not change with width; type and spacing tokens that do are on their own pages. --- # Spacing and shape > A short space scale, a 32/36/44 control height scale and radii. Every control reads the one height scale, so toolbars line up. URL: https://design.punji.app/foundations/spacing/ Section: Foundations (foundations) A short space scale, a control height scale (32, 36, 44) and radii. Every control reads the one height scale, so a Button, a Select and a SegmentedControl line up in a toolbar. ## When to use - Use `--pu-space-*` for gaps and padding. - Use `--pu-control-md` to align your own element with library controls. ## When not to use - Controls shorter than `--pu-tap-min` on touch screens. - Inventing radii: use `--pu-radius-control` or `--pu-radius-card`. ## Example: Scale ```tsx import { Cluster, Stack } from '@punji/ui/stack'; const steps = [1, 2, 3, 4, 16] as const; export default function Example() { return ( {steps.map((step) => ( --pu-space-{step} ))} ); } ``` ## Example: Control heights sm 32, md 36, lg 44 on the same row. ```tsx import { Button } from '@punji/ui/button'; import { Cluster } from '@punji/ui/stack'; export default function Example() { return ( your element at --pu-control-md ); } ``` ## Keyboard behaviour - Spacing is not interactive. ## Accessibility - `--pu-tap-min` (44px) is the minimum touch target the controls hold on phones. ## Responsive behaviour - Space tokens are fixed rem values; layouts reflow with container width, not with a different scale. --- # Typography > Two font stacks, a fluid text scale and tabular figures so money columns align. Mukta is included, so Devanagari renders without a layout shift. URL: https://design.punji.app/foundations/typography/ Section: Foundations (foundations) Two font stacks (body and display) and a fluid text scale. Figures use tabular digits so columns of money align. The stacks include Mukta, so Devanagari renders without a layout shift. ## When to use - Use `--pu-text-*` for sizes so type scales between phones and desktops. - Use tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) for anything numeric you lay out yourself. ## When not to use - Fixed pixel font sizes for body copy. - Proportional digits in tables of money. ## Example: Scale ```tsx import { Stack } from '@punji/ui/stack'; const sizes = ['xs', 'sm', 'base', 'lg'] as const; export default function Example() { return ( {sizes.map((size) => (

--pu-text-{size} The quick brown fox, NPR 12,34,567.89

))}

Tabular digits line up: 1,111.11 / 8,888.88

); } ``` ## Example: Devanagari Nepali text and digits in the same stack. ```tsx import { Stack } from '@punji/ui/stack'; export default function Example() { return (

रु १२,३४,५६७.८९ · नेपाल स्टक एक्सचेञ्ज

NPR 12,34,567.89 · Nepal Stock Exchange

Both lines use --pu-font-body; the stack includes Mukta for Devanagari.

); } ``` ## Keyboard behaviour - Type is not interactive. ## Accessibility - Sizes use rem and clamp(), so browser text-size settings are respected. - Set lang on Nepali content so screen readers choose the right voice. ## Responsive behaviour - The scale is fluid: it grows with the viewport between its clamp() bounds.

# Financial charts

Three charts and the pure math under them: `CandlestickChart`, `PerformanceChart`, `DepthChart` and `@punji/ui/chart-math`.
All are SVG drawn by this package (no chart library), display only, deterministic (the same props give the same pixels),
and take plain numbers. Styles: `@punji/ui/css/financial-charts.css` (in `styles.css`). The examples use synthetic NEPSE-style
data from `fixtures/market-data.ts`, not market data.

Shared behaviour:

- **Bad numbers are "no value", never zero.** Missing, `null`, `NaN` and infinities are gaps; the table says `none`.
- **One focus stop.** The plot is a named group (`aria-roledescription`, hint text). Left and Right step, Home and End jump,
  Escape clears. The focused point is announced in a polite live region and shown in a readout with a crosshair; the pointer
  does the same. A visually hidden `<table>` lists the values (the latest 500 candles or dates by default, `tableLimit`).
- **Colour is never the only cue.** Direction and series are also spelled out in words, dashes or shapes.
- **Responsive.** The SVG is as wide as its container (measured, `ResizeObserver`); heights are clamped.
- **Words are overridable** through `labels`; numbers through the `format*` props.
- Default price text is `NPR 487.50` from `Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN', { currency: 'NPR' })`. It is the platform formatter,
  not the exact bigint `@punji/ui/money` (which would add its weight to every chart). Pass `formatPrice` for exact money.

## CandlestickChart (`candlestick-chart`)

```tsx
<CandlestickChart label="NABIL daily" candles={candles} averages={[{ type: 'sma', window: 10 }]} />
```

Use it for OHLC per session with volume. Do not use it for a single line of closes (`PriceChart`) or order book size
(`DepthChart`).

| Prop | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `candles` | `{ date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', open, high, low, close, volume? }`, oldest first |
| `variant` | `'candles'` (default) or `'bars'` (OHLC ticks) |
| `volume` | volume pane; default on when any candle has a volume |
| `axis` | `'category'` (default, one slot per session) or `'time'` (spaced by date, gaps stay visible) |
| `hollowUp` | up candles as outlines, down filled |
| `convention` | per-chart override, `'green-up'` or `'red-up'`; default follows the theme (see below) |
| `averages` | `{ type: 'sma' \| 'ema', window, label? }[]`, computed over closes |
| `formatPrice`, `formatVolume`, `formatDate` | printing |
| `tableLimit` | latest N candles in the hidden table (default 500); the chart always uses all |
| `height`, `labels`, `testId` | height clamped to 140..640 |

Data rules: `low` must not exceed `open` or `close`, `high` must not be below them, every price finite, volume not
negative. A candle that breaks them is **not drawn**, is counted under the chart and stays in the table with the reason.
Across a width with less than 3px per candle, candles are aggregated (first open, last close, extreme high and low, summed
volume); the readout names the range. Non-trading days: the default category axis leaves no hole; `axis="time"` shows them.

Keyboard: Tab to the plot; Left and Right move one candle; Home and End; Escape. The live region says, for example
`14 Nov: up 0.28%, Open NPR 486.20, High …, Low …, Close NPR 487.50, Volume 41,000`.

## PerformanceChart (`performance-chart`)

```tsx
<PerformanceChart label="Portfolio against NEPSE" dates={dates} series={[portfolio, nepse]} periods={<MyPeriodSelector />} />
```

The first series is the portfolio (thickest line, with a gain and loss area against its start); the others are benchmarks
(colour and dash). By default every series is percent change from its own first real value (`normalize`), so rupees and index
points share a scale; `normalize={false}` plots raw values (`formatValue`, per-series `format`). `periods` is a slot for your
1M, 3M, 1Y, All control: slice `dates` and every series together. The legend is a row of toggle buttons (`aria-pressed`, Enter
or Space); the last visible series cannot be hidden. A line with more points than 2px each is reduced to each bucket's extremes.
A series whose first value is zero cannot be normalised and is not drawn. The hidden table lists the latest `tableLimit` dates
(default 500, as `CandlestickChart`; `labels.truncated` says how many are shown).

## DepthChart (`depth-chart`)

```tsx
<DepthChart label="NABIL depth" bids={bids} asks={asks} />
```

Cumulative bid and ask step areas around the mid price, with the spread under the chart. It takes the same `BookLevel`s as
`OrderBookDepth`, in any order: they are sorted best first, equal prices merged, invalid levels dropped. One side empty draws
that side only. A crossed book (best bid at or above best ask) draws both sides, shows no mid price and says so. Left and Right
move one price level; the readout says side, price, quantity and cumulative size.

## Gain and loss colour convention

Charts take up and down colours from the theme's `--pu-color-gain` and `--pu-color-loss`. Set the convention once with
`createTheme({ finance: 'red-up' })` (China, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan show a rise in red); every chart then renders up
in red, once. The `convention` prop on `CandlestickChart`, `PerformanceChart`, `MarketHeatmap`, `MarketBreadth` and
`PriceChange` is an absolute per-instance override that cannot double-swap with the theme. Direction is never colour alone:
candles can be hollow (`hollowUp`), and values carry signs, arrows and words. See
[THEMING.md](THEMING.md#gain-and-loss-colour-convention).

## Chart math (`chart-math`)

Pure, no React or browser (enforced by `check-boundaries`): `niceTicks`, `bandScale`, `timeScale`, `validateOhlc`,
`isValidOhlc`, `reduceCandles`, `aggregateByPeriod` (calendar weeks, months, quarters, years), `downsampleIndices`, `sma`, `ema`,
`rebase`, `rebaseOnto` (a late-starting series continues from a reference level), `cumulativeDepth`. Property-tested with
fast-check (`test/chart-math.test.ts`): ticks cover the domain, are ascending, evenly spaced and nice; downsampling keeps the
endpoints and the global minimum and maximum; candle aggregation keeps open, close, extremes and total volume; an SMA is the
mean of its window and blank until it fills; an EMA stays inside the data range; cumulative depth is monotone, best first and
independent of input order.

## Performance

Rendering 1,500 candles (jsdom, one render, including the aggregation and the hidden table's latest 500 rows) is measured in
`test/financial-charts.test.tsx` ("renders 1,500 and 2,000 candles quickly"). SVG output is bounded by the width: at most one
candle per 3px, so a 1,440px screen draws at most about 450 candles whatever the input length.

Under live ticks (one candle, date or level changing at a time) only the changed candle mark and table row re-render;
measured at 10, 100 and 1,000 ticks a second and at 1k to 100k points in [PERFORMANCE.md](PERFORMANCE.md#charts-and-live-tweening).
Feed a chart a new array with only the changed objects replaced (the forming candle), not a fresh copy of every object.

# Security

> What the package does to stay safe (no HTML from strings, one dependency, signed releases) and what stays yours: formula injection, masking, server validation.

URL: https://design.punji.app/get-started/security/
Section: Get started (get-started)

Components render text as text, the package has one reviewed runtime dependency and releases carry provenance. Client-side checks are conveniences: validate and authorise on the server, neutralise exports, and mask sensitive values before they reach a component.

## What the package does

From [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/20was/punji-ui/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

- No HTML from data: no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no `eval`, no inline event-handler strings. Components render text as text. `scripts/check-source.mjs` fails the build if one appears.
- One reviewed runtime dependency. React is a peer; the only bundled dependency is `@remotemerge/nepali-date-converter` (MIT, pinned exactly, no transitive dependencies), loaded only by the Bikram Sambat calendar.
- Releases you can verify: npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no stored token) with a provenance attestation and a CycloneDX SBOM per GitHub release. Check with `npm audit signatures` after you install.
- Hardened CI: pinned actions, least-privilege permissions, installs with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, a registry-only lockfile, CodeQL, zizmor and dependency review.

## Formula injection in exports

A spreadsheet treats a cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return as a formula, so exported user text such as `=HYPERLINK(...)` can run in the reader's Excel. `toCsv` therefore prefixes every text cell and header that starts with one of those characters with an apostrophe by default, following OWASP's guidance. A cell of JavaScript type `number` is exempt, because a finite number cannot contain a formula. `neutralizeFormulas: false` is for trusted, machine-generated data only. Details: [docs/EXPORT.md](https://github.com/20was/punji-ui/blob/main/docs/EXPORT.md) and the [CSV export](/utilities/csv-export/) page.

Neutralising in the browser reduces risk. It does not replace the server: neutralise on the server for any CSV the server generates or emails.

Export with a masked column:

```
import { toCsv, CSV_MIME } from '@punji/ui/export';
import { downloadText } from '@punji/ui/download';

interface Payment {
  payee: string; // user-typed text: may start with = + - @
  account: string; // sensitive
  amount: number;
}

/** Show only the last four characters. Do this before the value reaches a column, never after. */
const mask = (account: string) => `****${account.slice(-4)}`;

export function exportPayments(payments: readonly Payment[]): void {
  const csv = toCsv(
    payments,
    [
      // Text cells starting with = + - @ get a leading apostrophe by default (formula injection).
      { header: 'Payee', accessor: 'payee' },
      { header: 'Account', accessor: 'account', format: (value) => mask(String(value)) },
      { header: 'Amount', accessor: 'amount' },
    ],
    { bom: true },
  );
  // Runs in the browser only; the file never leaves it. The server still validates and authorises every export.
  downloadText('payments.csv', csv, CSV_MIME);
}
```

## Masking and what you pass in

A component prints exactly what it is given, and an export contains whatever you pass. Mask or omit sensitive values (account and card numbers, tax identifiers) before they reach a component or `toCsv`, and decide per role which columns a user may see or export. Hiding a column in the interface does not remove it from the data in the page.

## Client-side validation is not server validation

`CurrencyInput` limits what can be typed and parses to exact minor units, and the ledger helpers check that a journal balances. Both run in a browser that anyone can edit or bypass. Validate and authorise every amount, journal, total, period lock and permission again on the server, and show its error. A balanced trial balance on screen does not prove the books are right.

A form that trusts the server, not itself:

```
import { useState } from 'react';
import { CurrencyInput } from '@punji/ui/currency-input';
import { Button } from '@punji/ui/button';

// The input constrains what a person can type. That is a convenience, not a control: anyone can call your
// API directly. The server must parse and validate the amount again, check limits and permissions, and
// reject what is wrong. Show its error; do not assume the client check passed.
async function submit(minor: bigint): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; message: string }> {
  const response = await fetch('/api/transfers', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ amountMinor: minor.toString(), currency: 'NPR' }), // bigint has no JSON form
  });
  if (response.ok) return { ok: true };
  const body: unknown = await response.json().catch(() => null);
  const message = typeof body === 'object' && body !== null && 'message' in body ? String((body as { message: unknown }).message) : 'The transfer was not accepted.';
  return { ok: false, message };
}

export function TransferForm() {
  const [text, setText] = useState('');
  const [minor, setMinor] = useState<bigint | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | undefined>();
  return (
    <form
      onSubmit={async (event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        if (minor === null) return;
        const result = await submit(minor);
        setError(result.ok ? undefined : result.message);
      }}
    >
      <CurrencyInput
        label="Amount"
        currency="NPR"
        locale="en-IN"
        value={text}
        onValueChange={(change) => {
          setText(change.value);
          setMinor(change.state === 'valid' ? change.minorUnits : null);
        }}
        error={error}
      />
      <Button type="submit" disabled={minor === null}>
        Send
      </Button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## Content Security Policy

The package injects no scripts and loads no remote fonts or images itself. Some components write `style` attributes for computed sizes; if you use a strict `style-src`, test your pages. The package has not been checked against a strict CSP, so this is a check for you to run, not a guarantee.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue. Report privately through GitHub (Security, then Report a vulnerability, on the [repository](https://github.com/20was/punji-ui/security/advisories/new)) or email contact@punji.app with "SECURITY" in the subject. You get an acknowledgement within 3 working days and a first assessment within 10. Until 1.0 only the latest `0.x` receives fixes.

# Security policy

## Supported versions

Until 1.0, only the latest published `0.x` release receives fixes. After 1.0, the
latest minor of the current major does.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please do not open a public issue.

Report it privately through GitHub: **Security → Report a vulnerability** on this
repository (<https://github.com/20was/punji-ui/security/advisories/new>). If you
cannot use GitHub, email contact@punji.app with "SECURITY" in the subject.

You will get an acknowledgement within 3 working days and a first assessment
within 10. We will agree a disclosure date with you, credit you in the advisory
unless you prefer otherwise, and publish a fixed release before the details.

## What this package does to stay safe

- **One reviewed runtime dependency.** React is a peer; the only bundled dependency is `@remotemerge/nepali-date-converter` (MIT, pinned exactly, no transitive dependencies), loaded only by the Bikram Sambat calendar module. See [DEPENDENCY-AUDIT.md](DEPENDENCY-AUDIT.md).
- **No HTML from data.** No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no `eval`, no inline
  event-handler strings. Components render text as text.
- **Releases you can verify.** Every version is published from the
  [release workflow](./.github/workflows/release.yml) with npm Trusted Publishing
  (OIDC, no stored npm token) and carries a provenance attestation. Check it with
  `npm audit signatures` in your project, or on the package's npm page. Each
  GitHub release has a CycloneDX SBOM attached.
- **Hardened CI.** Actions pinned to commit SHAs, least-privilege `permissions`
  per job, no credentials persisted in checkouts, installs with
  `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, a lockfile that may resolve only to the npm registry
  over HTTPS with integrity hashes, registry signature checks, CodeQL, zizmor,
  dependency review on pull requests, and OpenSSF Scorecard.


---

# Trust and safety

> **UI is not enforcement.** The components here (and `OtpInput`, `PinPad`, `AccountNumber`, `LockedNote`, `EdisConfirmation` and the KYC helpers) are UX safeguards only. They do not enforce anything. Authorisation, step-up authentication, limits, payee checks, session expiry and validation must be enforced on the server. Hidden or disabled controls are not access control, and masking an account number only changes what is shown.

Money-movement patterns that most design systems leave to each bank: reading the amount back, checking the payee's
name, deliberate friction for risky actions, session timeouts, scam warnings and secret fields. Built for the fraud
that actually happens on payment screens (authorised push payment scams, look-alike payee names, coached victims)
and for the rules that now require some of it (UK Confirmation of Payee, EU Verification of Payee since October
2025, WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable, WCAG 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication).

| Export | Subpath | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `detectSpoofing`, `skeleton`, `areConfusable` | `@punji/ui/trust` | Pure name checks after Unicode UTS #39 |
| `TransferReview`, `ConfirmAmount` | `@punji/ui/transfer-review` | The confirm step: amount in figures and words, checked recipient, changed fields |
| `PayeeVerification` | `@punji/ui/payee-verification` | Match / close match / no match / unavailable result |
| `HoldToConfirm` | `@punji/ui/hold-to-confirm` | Press-and-hold or cooling-off friction |
| `SessionTimeoutWarning` | `@punji/ui/session-timeout` | WCAG 2.2.1 sign-out warning |
| `ScamWarning`, `SCAM_SCENARIOS` | `@punji/ui/scam-warning` | Scenario-specific scam interstitial |
| `SecureField`, `secureFieldAttributes` | `@punji/ui/secure-field` | Secret inputs with the right autofill and no value in the DOM |

Styles: `@punji/ui/css/trust.css` (also in `styles.css`).

**Other languages.** Every component here reads `PunjiLocaleProvider`; machine-drafted Nepali, Hindi and Bengali packs
(scam scenarios, spoofing sentences and amount in words included) are in `@punji/ui/locale/ne`, `/hi` and `/bn`. They
need native review before customers see them. See [LOCALISATION.md](LOCALISATION.md). For payment identifiers
(IBAN, card, UPI and others) see [PAYMENTS.md](PAYMENTS.md). The components also use `button.css`, `checkbox.css`,
`fields.css` and `overlay.css` when you import CSS per component.

**What this is not.** Nothing here decides whether a payment is fraud, verifies a payee or moves money. Your risk
engine decides when to show `ScamWarning` and `HoldToConfirm`; your bank or scheme answers the payee check; your
server re-checks amounts, payees and limits. These components make those decisions visible and hard to skip.

## Security boundary

1. **The amount is read back from the same bigint.** `ConfirmAmount` prints the figure with the exact money formatter
   and the words with `currencyAmountInWords`, both from the `amount` prop, so they cannot disagree. Words are
   automatic for English locales; pass `words` in other languages.
2. **Names are shown cleaned and checked.** `TransferReview` and `PayeeVerification` render names inside `<bdi>` after
   removing bidi controls, invisible characters and controls (`detectSpoofing(name).display`). A name with high-risk
   tricks, or one that looks like a saved payee without being it, blocks the confirm until the person ticks that
   they checked it. The custom `confirm` slot is not rendered until then.
3. **The spoofing check is a filter, not a verdict.** The confusable table is a focused subset (Cyrillic, Greek,
   Armenian, Cherokee and Latin look-alikes of Latin letters and digits), not the whole of `confusables.txt`.
   `risk: 'none'` means no known trick was found.
4. **Friction is a click away from bypass on a compromised device.** `HoldToConfirm` and the cooling-off delay stop
   accidents and give a coached person a moment; they are not authentication. Keep step-up checks on the server.
5. **Secrets stay out of the DOM.** `SecureField` pushes the value into the input's `value` property, never the
   `value` attribute that React writes for controlled inputs (CSS attribute selectors such as
   `input[value^="a"]` can read that out a character at a time). Nothing is written to data attributes, titles or
   labels, and the component never logs. Paste is allowed.
6. **The session timer only warns.** `SessionTimeoutWarning` shows what your server says (`expiresAt`); the server
   ends the session.

## Components

### detectSpoofing

`detectSpoofing(name, { known })` returns `{ risk, issues, scripts, display, skeleton, lookalikeOf? }`.

| Issue | Severity | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bidi-control` | high (overrides, isolates) / review (marks) | `Sita` + U+202E + `amrahs` |
| `invisible` | high | `Pay` + U+200B + `pal`; ZWJ/ZWNJ outside the scripts that need them |
| `control` | high | C0 and C1 controls |
| `confusable-characters` | high | Latin mixed with Cyrillic `а` (U+0430) |
| `lookalike` | high | `Paypa1` when `known` has `Paypal` |
| `whole-script-confusable` | review | `Рома`: every letter Cyrillic but Latin-looking |
| `mixed-script` | review | `Ramराम` (outside the UTS #39 highly restrictive sets) |
| `compatibility-form` | review | full-width or mathematical letters |
| `stacked-marks` | review | four or more combining marks in a row |
| `unusual-space` | review | no-break, doubled, leading or trailing spaces |

Single-script names in any script pass, and the zero-width joiner and non-joiner are accepted beside Devanagari,
Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Oriya, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Sinhala, Arabic, Syriac, Mongolian, Khmer and
Myanmar letters, where spelling needs them. `skeleton(text)` folds look-alikes (NFKC, mapped to Latin, lowercased, "rn"
read as "m"); `areConfusable(a, b)` is true when two different names share a skeleton.

### TransferReview and ConfirmAmount

Props: `amount`, `money` (a `MoneyFormatConfig`, as elsewhere in the kit: currency, locale, digits, exponent),
`currency` (optional; overrides `money.currency`, default NPR), `recipient` (`name`, `account`, `institution`),
`knownPayees`, `fee` (adds a total), `previousAmount`, `words`, `details` (`{ id, label, value, previous?, changed?
}`), `verification` (slot), `onConfirm` or `confirm` (slot), `onEdit`, `busy`, `labels`, `className`, `testId`.
Changed rows say "Changed (was …)" in text. The confirm button is `aria-disabled` while blocked, so it stays
focusable.

### PayeeVerification

`result`: `'checking' | 'match' | 'close-match' | 'no-match' | 'unavailable'`, with `enteredName`, `accountName`,
`onUseAccountName`, `onEdit`, `onProceed` (leave it out to block after no match). A match is a status; the other
results are alerts. Continuing after no match or unavailable needs the acknowledgement checkbox.

### HoldToConfirm

`mode: 'hold'` (default, `holdMs` 500 to 10000, default 1500) or `'cooling-off'` (`delaySeconds` 1 to 120, default
5). Holding Space or Enter works; key repeat is ignored; releasing early cancels and is announced. Remount with a new
React `key` to start again. Offer cooling-off rather than hold where people may not be able to hold a press.

### SessionTimeoutWarning

`expiresAt` (epoch ms), `warnBefore` (at least 20000, default 120000), `onExtend`, `onSignOut`, `onExpire`. An
`alertdialog`; focus starts on "Stay signed in" and returns; Esc stays signed in; the countdown is announced on
opening and at 60, 30 and 10 seconds only.

### ScamWarning

`scenario`: `'safe-account' | 'investment' | 'impersonation' | 'purchase' | 'romance' | 'urgent-request'`, or your
own `copy` (`{ summary, questions }`). `onCancel` is the primary action; `onProceed` (optional) needs the
acknowledgement, and `coolingOffSeconds` adds a delay after it. The heading takes focus on open.

### SecureField

`kind`: `current-password`, `new-password`, `one-time-code`, `pin`, `cc-number`, `cc-csc`, `cc-exp`,
`account-number`, `secret-answer`. Sets `type`, `autocomplete`, `inputmode`, `pattern`, and turns off spellcheck,
autocorrect and autocapitalise. Masked kinds get a Show/Hide button that hides again on blur and after
`revealSeconds` (default 30). `secureFieldAttributes(kind)` returns the same attributes for your own input.

## Testing

`test/trust.test.ts` (pure helpers) and `test/trust-components.test.tsx` (behaviour, keyboard, timers and axe for
every component). The SecureField test types a password and asserts it is nowhere in `innerHTML`.

# Versioning

This snapshot documents @punji/ui 0.2.0. The server data is generated from the repository and pinned to that version; reinstall or update punji-mcp to follow a newer release.

---

## Versioning policy (pre-1.0)


| Change | Bump |
| --- | --- |
| Breaking change | minor |
| Everything else | patch. Existing changesets also use minor for new API; follow CONTRIBUTING.md and say why in the summary |
| 1.0 | After the release-critical gaps in [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md) are closed |

From `0.0.0`, the pending minor changesets produce `0.1.0`. Only the latest `0.x` receives security fixes ([SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)). `.changeset/config.json`: `access: public`, `baseBranch: main`, `commit: false`.



---

Components are listed as `pre-1.0`: the API can change in a minor release until 1.0. Pin an exact @punji/ui version.

items.title: Financial calculations
items.description: Pure TypeScript for positions and ratios with no React or dependencies. Bigint ledger maths with a chosen rounding mode, plus display-only ratios.
items.summary: Pure TypeScript for positions and ratios: no React, no browser, no dependency. Ledger functions use bigint minor units and a rounding mode you choose; ratio functions are display-only numbers in percent units. Currency-agnostic.
use: Cost basis, realised and unrealised P&L, break-even and allocation.
Compute with these, then display with `MoneyDisplay`.
avoid: Floating-point arithmetic for money.
Treating rates as built in: rates are strings you take from a verified current source.

exports.name: computePosition
exports.description: Replay trades in order and return the open position. Throws when a sell exceeds the units held.

exports.name: valuePosition
exports.description: Mark a position to a price in minor units per unit. No selling fees are assumed.

exports.name: breakEvenPrice
exports.description:
Lowest price per unit at which selling everything recovers costBasis,
rounded up so selling at it never loses. `sellRate` models proportional
selling costs only, as a decimal fraction ('0.004'); tiered or flat fees
need the caller's own fee schedule. Null when nothing is held.
exports.signature: (costBasis: bigint, quantity: bigint, options?: { sellRate?: string | ExactRate | undefined; } | undefined) => bigint | null

exports.name: taxOnGain
exports.description:
Tax on a realised gain under a caller-supplied flat rule. Losses and zero
gains owe nothing here; loss carry-forward, holding-period tiers and
entity-specific rates belong to the caller's rule selection.

exports.name: allocation
exports.description:
Share of each holding in the total. Display percentages use the largest
remainder method, so a pie legend never reads 99.99% or 100.01%. Ties go to
the earlier item. Values must be non-negative: net-short books need their
own exposure view.
exports.signature: <K>(items: readonly AllocationInput<K>[], options?: { decimals?: number | undefined; } | undefined) => AllocationSlice<K>[]

exports.name: applyRate
exports.description: `amount × rate`, rounded. `rate` is a decimal fraction string, e.g. '0.0027' for 0.27%.
exports.signature: (amount: bigint, rate: string | ExactRate, mode: RoundingMode) => bigint

exports.name: divideRounded
exports.description: `numerator / denominator` rounded to an integer with the given mode. `half-up` rounds ties away from zero.
exports.signature: (numerator: bigint, denominator: bigint, mode: RoundingMode) => bigint

exports.name: percentageChange
exports.description:
`(current − previous) / previous` in percent. Null when the base is zero,
negative or not finite: a percentage against such a base misleads, so show
the absolute change instead.

exports.name: priceChange
exports.description: Absolute and percentage change together. Bigint inputs keep the absolute change exact.
exports.signature: { (current: bigint, previous: bigint): Change<bigint>; (current: number, previous: number): Change<number>; }

exports.name: returnOnCost
exports.description: `gain / cost` in percent; null when cost is not positive.

exports.name: cagr
exports.description:
Compound annual growth rate in percent. Null unless start > 0, end ≥ 0 and
years > 0. An end value of zero is a −100% CAGR.
exports.signature: (start: Amount, end: Amount, years: number) => number | null

exports.name: dividendYield
exports.description: Trailing or forward annual dividend per share over price, in percent. Null unless price > 0 and dividend ≥ 0.

exports.name: weightedAverage
exports.description: Σ(value × weight) / Σweight. Throws on negative or non-finite weights; null when total weight is zero.
