items.title: VirtualFinancialTable and TableExport
items.description: Virtualised table for 10,000+ financial rows with pinned and resizable columns, multi-column sort, live updates and formula-safe CSV export.
items.summary: VirtualFinancialTable takes the same typed columns as FinancialTable but draws only the rows in view, so a 10,000-trade floorsheet stays as fast as a page of 20. Columns pin left or right, resize by pointer or keyboard (widths come back through a callback to persist), and sort by several columns at once. Live rows keep the reader in place. TableExport turns the visible, all or selected rows into a CSV file with spreadsheet formulas neutralised. The table never sorts or filters your data.
use: Floorsheets, trade blotters, ledgers and statement lines with thousands of rows.
Live-updating rows: pass a new rows array per batch (per animation frame), keeping row objects that did not change.
Sort with `compareByRules(sort, accessors)` and the `sort` / `onSortChange` pair; Shift adds a column.
Persist widths from `onColumnResize` (for example with `useLocalStorage` and a validator) and pass them back as `columnWidths`.
avoid: Short tables (under a few hundred rows): `FinancialTable` keeps every row in the page for find-in-page, printing and phone stacking.
Rows of very different heights without `measureRows`: fixed heights are faster and steadier.
Exporting what the user cannot see without saying so: label the scopes, and keep `allRows` to data the user may download.

notes.title: Performance
points: 10,000 rows, Chromium on an Apple M4 Pro, `node scripts/bench-table.mjs` (method and full table: docs/PERFORMANCE.md).
Initial render: 1.7 ms to commit and 33 ms to first paint, against 75 ms and 406 ms for the plain FinancialTable.
Scrolling: 60 frames a second with about 22 rows in the DOM.
1,000 row updates a second, batched per frame: 0.6 ms per commit and a steady 60 FPS, against 41 ms per commit and 12 FPS for the plain table.
Without a dependency: about 5.1 kB gzip for the table, 1.8 kB for TableExport, in their own subpaths.

visible gap. `times` must be ascending. Marks are inset by half the typical
step so the first and last do not clip.
exports.signature: (times: readonly number[], start: number, end: number) => TimeScale

exports.name: validateOhlc
exports.description:
Checks one candle: every price finite, `low <= min(open, close)` and
`high >= max(open, close)`. A volume that is present must be finite and not
negative (a missing volume is fine). Returns the problems; empty means valid.

exports.name: reduceCandles
exports.description:
Aggregate consecutive candles into at most `max` buckets: the first open,
the last close, the highest high, the lowest low, the summed volume. Only
pass valid candles. Each bucket reports its first and last source index so a
caller can name the range.
exports.signature: (candles: readonly Ohlc[], max: number) => { candle: Ohlc; from: number; to: number; }[]

exports.name: downsampleIndices
exports.description:
Indices of the points to keep when a line has more than `max` of them:
the first, the last, and the minimum and maximum of each bucket between
(so the global extremes and every spike survive). Ascending, unique; the
whole range when it already fits. Missing values are never chosen as an
extreme. At most `max + 2` indices.
exports.signature: (values: readonly (number | null | undefined)[], max: number) => number[]

exports.name: sma
exports.description:
Simple moving average over `span` values. Position i is the mean of
values i-span+1..i, or `null` when fewer than `span` positions exist or
any value in the span is missing (a gap is never averaged as zero).
exports.signature: (values: readonly (number | null | undefined)[], span: number) => (number | null)[]

exports.name: ema
exports.description:
Exponential moving average, smoothing 2 / (span + 1), seeded with the mean
of the first `span` real values. A missing value gives `null` at its
position and leaves the running average untouched for the next real one.
exports.signature: (values: readonly (number | null | undefined)[], span: number) => (number | null)[]

exports.name: rebase
exports.description:
A series as percent change from its first finite value (that point is 0).
Missing stays `null`. A first value of zero cannot be a base: every point is
`null` rather than infinite.

exports.name: rebaseOnto
exports.description:
Like `rebase`, for a series that starts later than the one it is compared
with. On its first real date the series continues from where `reference`
(already in percent, for example `rebase(portfolio)`) stood that day, so a
benchmark that begins in March starts level with the portfolio instead of
pretending the portfolio was at 0% then. Growth compounds:
(1 + reference) x (1 + own) - 1. Without a real reference value on that day
it is plain `rebase`.
exports.signature: (values: readonly (number | null | undefined)[], reference: readonly (number | null | undefined)[]) => (number | null)[]

exports.name: aggregateByPeriod
exports.description:
Group candles into calendar periods: each period's candle has the first
open, the last close, the highest high, the lowest low and the summed
volume. Candles must be in date order; a period is a run of neighbours in
the same week, month, quarter or year, so a gap in time simply makes a
shorter period. A candle whose date is not a real "YYYY-MM-DD" is left out.
Weeks start on Sunday (NEPSE trades Sunday to Thursday); pass
`weekStartsOn` (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday) for another convention. Only pass
valid candles (see validateOhlc).
exports.signature: (candles: readonly DatedOhlc[], period: CalendarPeriod, options?: { weekStartsOn?: number | undefined; } | undefined) => PeriodBucket[]

exports.name: cumulativeDepth
exports.description:
Order book levels as running totals. Levels that are not a positive finite
price with a non-negative finite quantity are dropped. Bids are sorted high
to low, asks low to high (the best level first), then accumulated, so the
result does not depend on the order given. Equal prices are merged.
exports.signature: (levels: readonly { price: number; quantity: number; }[], side: "ask" | "bid") => DepthPoint[]

examples.title: A chart of your own
examples.note: Ticks, averages, percent change and data checks from chart-math; the drawing is plain SVG.

keyboard: Not a UI module.
accessibility: Nothing to render.
responsive: Not applicable.

notes.title: Guarantees
points: `aggregateByPeriod` groups dated candles into calendar weeks (Sunday start by default), months, quarters or years; `rebaseOnto` continues a late-starting series from a reference level.
`niceTicks` covers the domain (lo at or below min, hi at or above max) with steps of 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten.
`downsampleIndices` always keeps the first, last, global minimum and maximum, and never picks a gap as an extreme.
sma needs a full window of real values; a gap blanks only the windows that contain it.

items.title: CSV export
items.description: toCsv writes RFC 4180 CSV from typed rows, and downloadText saves it. Cells starting with =, +, -, @ are neutralised so spreadsheets do not run them.
items.summary: toCsv writes RFC 4180 CSV from typed rows and column definitions; downloadText hands the file to the browser. Cells that start with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return are neutralised by default so a spreadsheet will not run exported data as a formula.
use: Letting a reader export a table they can already see.
bom: true so Excel reads UTF-8.
avoid: Turning `neutralizeFormulas` off for any data that a user typed.
Exporting columns the reader is not allowed to see.

exports.name: toCsv
exports.description:
Serialise rows to RFC 4180 CSV.

Formula safety: text cells starting with = + - @, tab, CR, LF or a full-width = + - @
get a leading apostrophe.
Values that are typed `number` are exempt (a finite number prints only digits, "-", ".",
"e", "+", so negatives stay numeric); numeric-looking strings are not, unless the
column sets keepNumericText. Date, bigint and object values throw unless the column has
a `format`. Errors name the column header only, never the data.
exports.signature: <T>(rows: readonly T[], columns: readonly CsvColumn<T>[], options?: CsvOptions | undefined) => string

exports.name: downloadText
exports.description:
Browser-only: save text as a file through an object URL. Call from a user gesture
(click handler), never during render or on the server. The file name is sanitised and
the object URL is revoked shortly after the click. Nothing is sent over the network.
exports.signature: (filename: string, text: string, mime?: string | undefined) => void

examples.title: Formula injection
examples.note: Hostile cells before and after neutralisation.

responsive: Not applicable to the CSV; the trigger is an ordinary button.

notes.title: Security boundary
points: Client-side neutralisation reduces the risk of a spreadsheet running exported data. It does not replace server-side validation: validate and constrain what is stored, authorise what a user may export, and neutralise on the server for any CSV the server generates or emails.
Exports contain whatever you pass in. Mask or omit sensitive columns before calling `toCsv`.
A cell of type number is exempt (a finite number cannot hold a formula), so -5 stays numeric; the string "-5" is prefixed. Use `keepNumericText` on a column whose format emits plain machine numbers.
Date, bigint and object cells throw unless the column has a format function: there is no implicit locale or time zone, and the error names the column, never the value.
`downloadText` is browser-only and in its own subpath so server code never imports it. File names pass through `safeFilename`; nothing leaves the browser.
`neutralizeFormulas`: false is for trusted, machine-generated data only.

exports.name: Button
exports.description: The one button (design.punji.app/components/button).

props.name: variant

items.title: Hooks overview
items.description: Component-free, SSR-safe React hooks from @punji/ui/hooks, with stable callback identities and listeners and timers that clean up.
items.summary: Component-free React hooks from one subpath, @punji/ui/hooks (each also has its own). SSR-safe: nothing touches the browser while rendering. Callback identities are stable and timers and listeners clean up.
use: `useDebounce` for search, `useLocalStorage` for persisted preferences, `useClipboard` for copy buttons.
`usePagination`, `useTableSelection` and `useColumnVisibility` beside `DataTable`.
avoid: Storing tokens, secrets or account data in web storage: any script on the origin can read it.
Using `useHydrated` to hide server-renderable content.

exports.name: useDebounce
exports.description: Trailing-edge debounced copy of `value`. The first render returns `value` unchanged.

exports.name: useDebouncedCallback
exports.description:
Debounce a callback. The returned function keeps its identity while `delayMs` and
`leading` are unchanged, always calls the latest `callback`, and cancels on unmount.
exports.signature: <A extends unknown[]>(callback: (...args: A) => void, delayMs: number, options?: DebouncedCallbackOptions | undefined) => DebouncedFunction<A>

exports.name: useThrottle
exports.description:
Throttled copy of `value`: the first change goes through at once, later changes update
at most once per `intervalMs`, and the latest value is delivered on the trailing edge.
The first render returns `value` unchanged.

exports.name: useControllableState
exports.description:
One state for components that can be controlled (`value`) or uncontrolled
(`defaultValue`). `onChange` fires for every request in both modes. The setter
accepts a value or an updater, and keeps its identity for the component lifetime.
Switching between controlled and uncontrolled warns in development.
exports.signature: <T>({ value, defaultValue, onChange, name }: ControllableStateOptions<T>) => [T, (next: T | ((previous: T) => T)) => void]

exports.name: usePrevious
exports.description:
The value `value` had before its latest change (not before the latest render),
or `initial` until the first change. Uses render-phase state, no ref reads.
exports.signature: { <T>(value: T): T | undefined; <T, I>(value: T, initial: I): I | T; }

exports.name: useToggle
exports.description:
Boolean state with stable setters. `toggle()` flips; `toggle(true)` sets. Non-boolean
arguments (such as a click event passed straight from onClick) flip.
exports.signature: (initial?: boolean | undefined) => [boolean, (next?: unknown) => void, (value: boolean) => void]

exports.name: useClipboard
exports.description:
Copy to the clipboard through the async Clipboard API. It does not fall back to
execCommand. Treat `copied` as a short-lived confirmation, not proof of content.

exports.name: useLocalStorage
exports.description:
JSON state in localStorage, shared across components and tabs. Do not store secrets,
tokens or account data: any script on the origin can read this. `defaultValue` and
`validate` should be stable references (module constants).

exports.name: useSessionStorage
exports.description: As useLocalStorage, scoped to the tab's sessionStorage.

exports.name: useClickOutside
exports.description:
Call `handler` when a pointerdown lands outside every given element. Pass one ref per
DOM subtree, including portalled content (portals are not DOM descendants). Listens in
the capture phase so handlers that stop propagation do not hide the event.
exports.signature: (refs: readonly RefObject<Element | null>[] | RefObject<Element | null>, handler: (event: PointerEvent) => void, { enabled }?: ClickOutsideOptions | undefined) => void

exports.name: usePagination
exports.description:
Pagination state. When `total` shrinks, the reported page is clamped at once; the
stored request is kept, so growth restores it. The setters clamp what they are given.
exports.signature: ({ total, page, defaultPage, onPageChange, pageSize, defaultPageSize, onPageSizeChange }: PaginationOptions) => PaginationState

exports.name: useTableSelection
exports.description:
Row selection by id. Selection survives page changes; page and all-row toggles only
touch the ids they are given. Ids are opaque strings and are never logged.
exports.signature: ({ pageIds, allIds, selected: controlled, defaultSelected, onChange }: TableSelectionOptions) => TableSelectionState

exports.name: useColumnVisibility
exports.description:
Which table columns show. Unknown ids are ignored and at least one column always stays
visible. Persist by feeding `hidden`/`onChange` from useLocalStorage with a validator.
exports.signature: ({ columns, hidden: controlled, defaultHidden, onChange }: ColumnVisibilityOptions) => ColumnVisibilityState

exports.name: useMediaQuery
exports.description:
SSR and hydration use serverMatch; client renders follow the actual query.
Supply the same serverMatch on server and client. Prefer CSS for visual layout.

exports.name: useHydrated
exports.description:
False on the server and initial hydration pass; true after hydration.
Client-only rendering returns true immediately. No timers or global flag.

exports.name: useStableOrder
exports.description:
Keep rows still during value updates; re-sort when sortId or membership changes.
Input must already be sorted. keyOf returns a unique stable string per row.
Output contains the latest row objects and never mutates the input array.
exports.signature: <T>(sorted: readonly T[], keyOf: (row: T) => string, sortId: string) => T[]

exports.name: useHotkeys
exports.description:
Bind keyboard shortcuts while the component is mounted. The first matching entry wins. A combination with a
modifier fires in text fields (Command-K from the search box); a plain key does not, unless `allowInInputs`.
exports.signature: (hotkeys: readonly Hotkey[], { enabled }?: HotkeysOptions | undefined) => void

exports.name: formatHotkey
exports.description: A combination as people read it: "⌘K" on Apple platforms, "Ctrl+K" elsewhere. Several combinations are joined with " or ".

exports.name: matchHotkey
exports.description:
Whether a key event matches a combination. `mod` is Command when `apple` is true, Control otherwise. Modifiers must
match exactly, except Shift on a symbol key: `?` is Shift+/ on most layouts, so `'?'` matches with or without a
Shift the combination did not name.
exports.signature: (event: KeyEventLike, combo: string, apple?: boolean | undefined) => boolean

exports.name: Hotkey
exports.description:
Keyboard shortcuts for an application screen: `mod+k` opens a palette, `b` starts a buy, `?` shows help. One
listener on the document, handlers read through a ref (so passing a new array each render costs nothing), and plain
keys never fire while the person types in a field, a select or an editable region, or while an IME is composing.

props.name: keys
props.description:
The combination: modifiers and one key joined by `+`, case-insensitive. Modifiers are `mod` (Command on Apple
platforms, Control elsewhere), `ctrl`, `meta`, `alt` and `shift`. The key is a `KeyboardEvent.key` value: a letter,
a digit, a symbol (`?`, `/`) or a name (`escape`, `enter`, `arrowup`). Several combinations: `'mod+k, /'`.

props.name: handler
props.description: Called with the event. The default action is prevented unless `preventDefault` is false.

props.name: allowInInputs
props.description: Fire while focus is in a text field too. Default: true for a combination with `mod`, `ctrl`, `meta` or `alt`, false otherwise.

props.name: preventDefault
props.description: Prevent the browser's default for a matched key. Default true.

examples.title: useDebounce
useClipboard
examples.note: This site's own copy button uses it.

examples.title: useLocalStorage
examples.note: This site's theme switch uses it with a validator.

examples.note: Press B or S with focus outside the field; Ctrl+J or ⌘J works from inside it too. The trading terminal app binds its shortcuts this way.

keyboard: Hooks have no UI. `useHotkeys` ignores plain keys while focus is in a text field, a select or an editable region, and during IME composition; combinations with a modifier fire everywhere.

responsive: `useMediaQuery` takes a server fallback; use CSS for purely visual layout.

notes.title: Storage safety
points: Stored data is untrusted. `validate` is required: a stored value is returned only if it parses and passes it; otherwise you get `defaultValue` and error: "invalid".
Write failures (quota, serialize, unavailable) are returned in `error`, never thrown during render.

items.title: StockTable
items.description: A React stock table for NEPSE or any market: symbol, LTP, change, volume, turnover and a trend line. You own the data and sort; prices are exact bigint.
items.summary: A full quote board: symbol over name, LTP, change, volume, turnover and an optional trend line, built on DataTable. The caller owns the data and the sort (sortQuotes plus controlled props); nothing here fetches, filters or re-sorts. Prices are exact bigint minor units, and a missing value is a dash with a spoken "No value", never zero.
use: A whole market or sector board where people sort and compare.
Row selection and column choice (with `useColumnVisibility`).
Live prices fed from your own socket or query, with `live` to count and flash each new LTP.
avoid: A short top-N list: use `MarketMovers`. The stocks a person follows: use Watchlist. Arbitrary records: use `FinancialTable`.
Search and pagination: they are not built in. Filter first, sort the matches, then slice.
Passing floating-point prices: the types require bigint minor units.

props.name: quotes

props.name: sort

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called with the sort a click on a column head asks for: a new column starts ascending for the symbol and descending for figures, and a repeat click on the sorted column flips its direction (the rule `nextQuoteSort` implements). The table does not reorder rows: sort `quotes` yourself and pass `sort` back.

props.name: money

props.name: convention
props.description: Per-instance override of which hue means up: 'green-up' or 'red-up' (absolute, never a second swap on top of the theme). Default: follow the theme's gain and loss colours (`createTheme({ finance })`), which is the one place to set the convention.

props.name: changeLabels
props.description: Spoken direction words for the change.

props.name: selectedSymbols

props.name: onSelectedSymbolsChange
props.description: Called with the new list of selected symbols when a row checkbox changes. Keep it in state and pass it back as `selectedSymbols`.

props.name: selectLabel
props.description: Accessible name of a row checkbox. Default `Select NABIL`.

exports.name: rankMovers
exports.description:
The top `limit` quotes of a kind.
- gainers: change above zero, largest percent first.
- losers: change below zero, largest fall first.

the input order. Does not mutate the input.

exports.name: getMarketSession
exports.description:
What the market is doing at `now` under `schedule`.

- A date in `holidays` is `holiday` all day, whatever the windows say.
- Inside a window the state is that window's; otherwise `closed` (nights, weekends).
- `options.halted` turns an `open` or `pre-open` market into `halted`. Halts come from the
  exchange, not the clock, so the caller passes them in (for example from a feed).

Throws RangeError for an unknown time zone, a malformed time or date, or an invalid `now`.
exports.signature: (now: number | Date, schedule: MarketSchedule, options?: { halted?: boolean | undefined; } | undefined) => MarketSession

exports.name: nepseSchedule
exports.description:
AN EXAMPLE, NOT AUTHORITY. Hours that Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) has used for its equity
market: pre-open 10:30 to 11:00 and continuous trading 11:00 to 15:00, Sunday to Thursday,
Asia/Kathmandu. The exchange changes its hours and announces holidays by notice. Verify the
hours against NEPSE's current notice before relying on this, and supply `holidays` yourself;
none are built in.

props.description: IANA time zone, for example 'Asia/Kathmandu' or 'America/New_York'.

props.name: sessions
props.description: The pre-open and open windows. A moment inside none of them is `closed`.

props.name: holidays
props.description: Dates on which the market is closed all day (state `holiday`). Keep them current: none are built in.

props.name: state
props.description: What the market is doing at `now`.

props.name: label
props.description: The session window's label, or the holiday's name, when there is one.

props.description: The date and time on the exchange's clock at `now`.

props.description: The time on the exchange's clock at `now`, 'HH:mm'.

notes.title: Schedule caveats
points: `nepseSchedule` encodes pre-open 10:30 to 11:00 and continuous trading 11:00 to 15:00, Sunday to Thursday, Asia/Kathmandu, with no holidays. It is an example. Verify against NEPSE's current notice and supply holidays: { ...`nepseSchedule`, holidays }.

Times are read in the schedule's IANA zone with Intl, so daylight saving is the platform's. days are 0 (Sunday) to 6; a window includes its start and excludes its end; a date in holidays is "holiday" all day.
halted: true turns open or pre-open into halted. next is the next change among open, pre-open and closed within ten days; a halt is never predicted.
`getMarketSession` throws `RangeError` for an unknown zone, a malformed time or date, a window ending before it starts, or an invalid now.

items.title: MarketBreadth
items.description: Market breadth in React: advances, declines and unchanged as one split bar with counts, shares and the A/D ratio, plus circuit hits or 52-week highs.
items.summary: How many stocks rose, fell and stayed flat: one bar split in three, the counts and their shares printed beside it, and the advance/decline ratio. Optional extra counts sit under the bar (stocks at their circuit limits, 52-week highs and lows, scrips traded). `breadthOf` counts it from quotes; a stock with no price counts as unchanged, as exchanges report it. Direction is said in words and arrows, never by colour alone, and the declines are hatched in forced colours.
use: The breadth line of a market overview, beside the index cards.
A header row (`size="sm"`) above a quote board or a sector page.
avoid: Weighted breadth (by turnover or market cap): it counts stocks, one each. Use `MarketHeatmap` for weight.
A history of breadth over days: draw that with `ColumnChart`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the figure ("NEPSE breadth").

props.name: extra
props.description: More counts listed under the bar (circuit hits, 52-week highs and lows, traded scrips).

props.name: showRatio
props.description: Print the advance/decline ratio. Default true.

props.name: convention
props.description: Per-instance override of which hue means up: 'green-up' or 'red-up' (absolute, never a second swap on top of the theme). Default: follow the theme's gain and loss colours (`createTheme({ finance })`), which is the one place to set the convention.

props.name: loading
props.description: Placeholders with a spoken status instead of the figures.

props.name: size
props.description: 'sm': a thinner bar and smaller type, for a header row.

props.name: labels
props.description: Words in the reader's language.

props.name: formatCount
props.description: Format a count. Default grouped en-IN.

props.name: testId
props.description: Sets `data-testid` on the figure.

props.name: advances
props.description: Stocks whose price is above the previous close.

props.name: declines
props.description: Stocks whose price is below the previous close.

props.name: unchanged
props.description: Stocks that traded at the previous close, or did not trade.

exports.name: breadthOf
exports.description:
Counts advances, declines and unchanged from quotes (price and previous close in minor units). A quote with a
missing price or previous close counts as unchanged, as exchanges report a stock that did not trade.
exports.signature: (quotes: readonly { ltp: bigint | null; previousClose: bigint | null; }[]) => Breadth

exports.name: advanceDeclineRatio
exports.description: Advances over declines, or null when nothing declined (the ratio is undefined).

props.name: advances
props.description: Stocks whose price is above the previous close.

props.name: declines
props.description: Stocks whose price is below the previous close.

props.name: unchanged
props.description: Stocks that traded at the previous close, or did not trade.

props.description: Stable key.

props.description: What is counted ("At upper circuit", "52-week highs").

keyboard: Not interactive: nothing takes focus.
accessibility: The bar is an image named with every count ("45 advances, 30 declines, 5 unchanged of 80"); the counts are also printed as a description list.
Arrows and words carry direction; `convention="red-up"` swaps the colours only.
Loading is a status with a spoken name; the empty state says why there is nothing.
responsive: The bar fills its container; the counts wrap onto more lines when narrow.

items.title: PriceChart
items.description: A compact accessible line chart for a short labelled series. Missing values break the line instead of drawing zero, with a data table for every point.
items.summary: A compact line chart for a short labelled series. Straight segments, gaps stay gaps (a missing value breaks the line, never drawn as zero), fixed SVG proportions, and an exact-value data table for every point. Not for high-volume intraday series.
use: A closing-price line for a few weeks or months.
Anywhere the exact numbers must stay reachable as a table.
avoid: Thousands of ticks: it draws every point.
Periodic totals: use `ColumnChart`. A tiny trend beside a figure: use Sparkline.

exports.name: PriceChart
exports.description: Straight segments, gaps stay gaps, fixed aspect ratio, and an accessible data table.

props.name: points
props.description: The observations in order. With no finite value at all the chart is replaced by an empty state titled `missingLabel`.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the chart (its caption and the image's accessible name).

props.name: formatValue
props.description: Formats a value for the high and low labels and the data table.

props.name: dataLabel
props.description: The words on the disclosure that opens the data table. Default 'View chart data'.

props.name: missingLabel
props.description: Shown for a missing value in the data table, and as the title of the empty state when nothing is published. Default 'Unavailable'.

props.name: label
props.description: The observation's name (a date), in order, oldest first; printed in the data table.

props.name: value
props.description: The value at that label. Null or not finite is a gap: the line breaks and the table shows `missingLabel`.

examples.title: Series with a gap
examples.note: 6 Nov has no value: the line breaks and the table says so.

examples.title: Edge cases
examples.note: One observation and a series with nothing published.

keyboard: The data table sits in a native details disclosure: Tab to its summary, Enter or Space opens it. The drawing itself is not interactive.
accessibility: The drawing is an image named by label; the exact value at every label is in the data table behind the `dataLabel` disclosure, with `missingLabel` where there is none.
One line, no colour-only encoding. With no finite value at all the chart is replaced by an empty state.
responsive: The SVG keeps its aspect ratio and scales to the container width.

items.title: Sparkline
items.description: A small trend line with no axes for use beside a printed figure. Missing values are dropped, never zero, and long series keep each bucket's extremes.
items.summary: A small trend line with no axes, for use beside a printed figure. Missing and non-finite values are dropped, not drawn as zero; fewer than two real values draw a dashed rule; long series are reduced to each bucket's extremes so a spike survives. Decorative unless you give it a label.
use: Beside a price in a table row, watchlist or card.
fluid to fill a cell while keeping its aspect.
avoid: The only source of a number: print the figure beside it.
Inspection on hover: a sparkline has none. Use `PriceChart` or `ColumnChart` for readable values.

exports.name: Sparkline
exports.description:
Memoised: a watchlist row that re-renders with a new price but the same
closes array skips the line (no reduce, no path). Safe in a Server
Component (memo is part of React's server build); no hooks, no client code.

props.name: values
props.description: Closes, oldest first. Missing, null and non-finite entries are dropped, not drawn as zero.

props.name: width
props.description: The drawing's own size in px (the aspect ratio when `fluid`).

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the drawing in px (with `width`, the aspect ratio when `fluid`). Default 28.

props.name: tone
props.description: Default: gain when the last value is above the first, loss when below, flat when equal.

props.name: fluid
props.description: Fill the container's width, keeping the aspect ratio; strokes do not scale.

props.name: maxPoints
props.description: Series longer than this are reduced to their extremes per bucket (first and last always kept). Default 120, least 8.

props.name: label
props.description: Names it (role img); decorative without.

props.name: testId
props.description: Sets `data-testid` on the drawing.

exports.name: reduceSeries
exports.description: Keep the first and last points and the low and high of each bucket, in order.

examples.title: Tones
examples.note: The default tone follows first versus last; tone overrides it.

examples.title: Edge cases
examples.note: Gaps, one value, none, 400 points reduced with a spike kept, and fluid.

keyboard: Not interactive.
accessibility: Decorative (`aria-hidden`) by default; label turns it into an image with that name.
Direction is never carried by the line colour alone: the figure beside it states it.
responsive: Fixed size by default; fluid fills the container's width, strokes do not scale.

items.title: CompanySearch
items.description: One field for symbol or name with ranked in-memory suggestions, as a finder or a picker, with a full-height sheet on phones. Nothing is fetched while typing.
items.summary: One field (symbol or name) with ranked suggestions under it, searched in memory over the options you pass, so nothing is fetched while typing. A finder opens the chosen company; a picker (give it a value) shows the pick and turns into the search when focused. On a phone the picker opens a full-height sheet.
use: A "find any company" field a page leads with, or an add field on a watchlist.
A symbol picker in a form (alerts, holdings, backtests).
avoid: A server-side search over a huge list: it ranks the options you pass in memory.
A plain choice from a few options: use Select.

props.description: The companies to search, each a symbol and a name. Ranked in memory: exact symbol, symbol prefix, name word prefix, then symbol contains.

props.name: testId
props.description: Sets `data-testid` on the input (in the phone sheet: `<id>-sheet`, `<id>-sheet-input`, `<id>-sheet-close`).

props.name: optionTestId

props.name: listTestId
props.description: Sets `data-testid` on the list of suggestions.

props.name: hideLabel
props.description: Hide the label visually (it stays the field's name).

props.name: size
props.description: 'lg' (default): the 52px finder a page leads with; 'md': the 40px field in a header or a form; 'sm': 36px, level with a Select and a SegmentedControl at md in one control row (44px on a phone, the touch minimum).

props.name: clearOnOpen

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong, under the field.

props.name: loading

props.name: initialQuery

props.name: closeLabel

Escape clears the query, then leaves. In a picker, Escape puts the pick back.
"/" focuses a finder when nothing else is being typed in (set shortcut to null to turn it off).
accessibility: A visible label (or `hideLabel`) is the field's accessible name.
The input is a combobox over a listbox of options; the active option is exposed with `aria-activedescendant`.
The "no match" line is a status and an error under the field is an alert; loading sets `aria-busy`.
responsive: Under 768px a tapped picker opens a full-height sheet with one input and the matches. Sizes sm, md (headers and forms) and lg (a page's lead field, the default).

items.title: Breakdown
items.description: How a total is made: one row per part and the total ruled off, as a description list. It does no arithmetic and knows no fee or tax rule.
items.summary: How a total is made: one row per part (label, optional note, amount) and the total ruled off, as a description list. It does no arithmetic and knows no fee or tax rule: you compute and format every amount (a string, or a MoneyDisplay for an exact one) and say which row is the total.
use: The summary of a sale or purchase form, from the amount down to what is received.
live when the figures change as the form is filled.
avoid: Computing fees or tax inside it: it only lays out what you give it.
A plain label and value list with no total: use `FactList`.

items.title: ShareBar, ShareDonut and DistributionBar
items.description: Shares of one whole as a stacked bar (ShareBar), a ring (ShareDonut) or counts on a five-step scale (DistributionBar), each with a worded legend.
items.summary: Shares of one whole as a stacked bar with a legend (ShareBar), as a ring with a count in the middle (ShareDonut, with ShareLegend alone), or counts on a five-step scale (DistributionBar). Each needs a label that says the shares in words, and every share has a legend row with its name and value, so tone is never the only carrier of meaning.
use: Sector or asset allocation of a portfolio.
A legend item as a button to filter or open a sector (`onSelect`).
`DistributionBar` for how many items sit at each of five steps (ratings, risk levels).
avoid: Using the bar instead of a printed figure: print the value in the legend.
More than twelve categorical tones: anything after is "rest", the only grey.
Exact comparison: use a table or `ColumnChart`.

items.title: MeterBar and RangeBar
items.description: MeterBar lays parts on one track with a benchmark marker; RangeBar shows where a value sits among others. Decorative unless labelled; print figures beside them.
items.summary: MeterBar lays parts end to end on one track, with an optional marker for a benchmark on the same scale. RangeBar shows where a value sits among other values: a fill or a span, and marks whose labels sit under the mark. Both are decorative unless you give them a label: print the figures they draw beside them.
use: `MeterBar`: a gain and its dividends, proceeds and what fees take, a limit used.
`RangeBar`: a 52-week range, a month inside a year, a company among its peers.
avoid: Using either as the only place a number appears.
`RangeBar` rows that do not share a domain when they are meant to be compared: give them the same domain.

props.name: parts
props.description: The segments laid end to end: each a `value` on the scale and a `tone`.

props.name: max
props.description: The scale's whole (default: the parts' sum).

props.name: marker
props.description: Where a marker sits, on the same scale.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the bar (an img); without it the bar is decorative.

props.name: testId
props.description: Sets `data-testid` on the bar.

props.name: head
props.description: The row over the track: what the two ends or the two values are.

props.name: fill
props.description: The track fills up to this value.

props.name: span
props.description: The track is filled between these two values (a month's low and high) instead of from the start; give the domain so rows share one scale.

props.name: marks
props.description: The marks on the track, each a value, a kind and an optional label.

props.name: domain
props.description: The track's ends; default: the smallest and largest of fill, span and marks.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the bar (an img) with its figures in words; without it the bar is decorative, so print the figures in `head` or beside it.

props.name: legend
props.description: Three labels in fixed places under the track (the low end, the middle, the high end), instead of labels under the marks.

props.name: testId
props.description: Sets `data-testid` on the bar.

props.name: value
props.description: Where the mark sits, on the same scale as the domain.

props.name: kind

strong: the value itself (a price); accent: a reference (an alert); dot: the value as a round mark among
others (a company among its peers); tick: a quiet reference (a median); edge: a label only, at an end.

props.name: label
props.description: Printed under the mark. Hidden when the bar has a `label` of its own.

items.title: HeadlineFigure and FigureChip
items.description: A page's lead figure: a quiet label, the figure large, and changes as FigureChips. The figure never truncates and chip tint never carries direction.
items.summary: A page's or a view's lead figure: a quiet label, the figure large ("Rs" smaller and muted), and the changes as FigureChips. The figure never truncates and a long label wraps. A chip's tint never carries direction: write the sign and words in its text.
use: The portfolio value at the top of a page, with today and this week as chips.
`labelAction` for a small control on the label line, such as an amounts toggle.
avoid: More than one per view: for the one figure to act on inside a card use `SummaryFigure`.
A chip whose text has no sign or word: add `srLabel` ("Loss") or put the sign in the text.

items.title: KeyStats and FactList
items.description: KeyStats lays a panel's facts as label-over-value cells; FactList is one column of label-and-value lines. Unknown values say so in words, never zero.

FactList is one column of label-and-value lines under a small title. A value that is not known says so in words (empty, quiet), never a dash or a zero. Both are description lists.
use: Fundamentals, a session's open/high/low/close, a company's facts.
`FactList` for a few facts on a tint, or stacked on a phone.
avoid: A figure with a meter: use `MetricTile`.
A long or sortable list: use a table.
Colour-only signs: a tone only tints, so put the sign in the value.

props.name: empty
props.description: The words for a value that is not known ("Not published").

props.name: label
props.description: Names the list for screen readers when it has no heading.

props.name: loading

props.name: testId

notes.title: Security boundary
points: `ledgerToCsv` goes through `toCsv`, so formula neutralisation stays on for every text cell: an account, reference or description such as =HYPERLINK(...) is exported with a leading apostrophe. Amounts are exact decimal text at the currency's scale and dates are ISO, so neither can start a formula.

Client-side neutralisation reduces the risk of a spreadsheet running exported data. It does not replace server-side validation: validate what is stored, authorise what a user may export, and neutralise on the server for any CSV the server generates or emails.
An export contains whatever you pass in: omit or mask accounts the reader may not see before calling `ledgerToCsv`.

A browser can be edited by anyone. The server that stores the books must validate every amount, journal and total again (balanced journals, no negatives, period locks, permissions). A balanced trial balance does not prove the books are right.

exports.name: maskAccountNumber
exports.description:
Hide all but the last `visible` characters of an account number. Separators in the input are dropped first, so
"0123 4567 8901 2345" and "0123456789012345" mask the same. It never reveals more than `visible` characters, and never
more than half the number: "1234" with visible 4 shows "••34". Empty or non-string input gives ''. The result keeps the
length (one mark per hidden character); if the length itself is sensitive, show a fixed placeholder instead.

exports.description: Remove spaces, hyphens, dots and underscores and any control or invisible character. Non-strings become ''.

exports.name: isValidIban
exports.description:
Check an IBAN's shape and its ISO 7064 mod-97 check digits. Generic on purpose: it accepts any two-letter prefix and 15
to 34 characters, and does not know which countries issue IBANs or how long theirs are. Passing means "no typing slip",
not "this account exists": confirm on the server.

exports.name: formatIban
exports.description: An IBAN in blocks of four ("GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32"). Returns '' for non-strings. It does not validate; use `isValidIban`.

exports.name: normalizeIban
exports.description: Uppercase an IBAN and drop spaces and separators. Non-strings become ''.

exports.name: formatTransactionReference
exports.description:
Make a transaction reference safe and tidy to print: control, zero-width and bidirectional characters are removed (they can
reorder or hide text), whitespace is collapsed and trimmed, and a long reference can be shortened from the middle. The
reference is data from outside; React escapes it, and this keeps lookalike tricks out. Non-strings become ''.

exports.name: formatTimestamp
exports.description: Format an instant (a Date, epoch milliseconds, or an ISO string with an offset or Z). Returns null for anything that is not a real instant.
exports.signature: (value: string | number | Date | null | undefined, options?: TimestampOptions | undefined) => FormattedTimestamp | null

exports.name: transactionsToCsv
exports.description: Exact CSV of transactions in the order given. Amounts such as "-1250.50" stay numeric; text starting = + - @ gets an apostrophe.
exports.signature: (transactions: readonly BankTransaction[], options?: TransactionsCsvOptions | undefined) => string

exports.name: directionOf
exports.description: Money out is a debit, money in a credit (the account holder's view).

notes.title: Security boundary
points: Masking never reveals more than visible characters and never more than half the number. It keeps the length (one mark per hidden character); if the length is sensitive, show a fixed placeholder.

Everything here is generic: no bank list, no account-length rules, no country rules. Rules for a specific bank or scheme are yours, and the server must check them again. Client-side validation never replaces server-side validation.
`formatTimestamp` refuses an ISO string with no offset (it would be read in the host's zone) and falls back to UTC, naming it, for an unknown zone.

keyboard: Tab moves into and out of the field; the label is a real <label>, so a click on it focuses the input.

`NumberField` with `step` or `steppers`: `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` add or subtract one step, Shift or `PageUp`/`PageDown` ten steps, `Home` and `End` jump to `min` and `max`. The - and + buttons are out of the Tab order.
`SymbolField`: `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp` move through the matches, Enter picks the active one, Esc closes the list (the typed text stays).
`DateField` and the textarea use the browser's own keyboard behaviour.
accessibility: The label is always rendered; `hideLabel` keeps it for screen readers only (kit-sr).
An error is a `role="alert"` line linked by `aria-describedby` and sets `aria-invalid`; a hint is linked the same way. An error replaces the hint.
`SymbolField` is an ARIA combobox with a listbox, `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-expanded`.
lg is 44px (forms, the default) so a phone does not zoom on focus; md is 36px for toolbars.
responsive: Fields fill their container; put them in a grid or stack. lg keeps the 44px touch target on phones.

notes.title: Limits
points: There is no separate quantity component. `NumberField` with `step`, `min`, `max` and `steppers` is the spin button (role spinbutton, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuetext` carrying the exact string). Stepping is exact decimal arithmetic through `stepDecimal`, clamps into the limits and leaves typed text outside them alone for you to flag; unfinished text such as "12." is not stepped. Hold-to-repeat is not implemented.

`NumberField` shows the text exactly as typed and sets `inputMode` ("numeric" with integer, otherwise "decimal"). `onValueChange` reports the text parsed (grouping commas and Devanagari digits accepted, no rounding) as a plain decimal string or a reason it is not a number yet. It does not check ranges or set the error for you; for money, parse to minor units or use `CurrencyInput`.
The value is always a string and `onChange` gives a string. `DateField`'s value is YYYY-MM-DD, the native date input's format; for Bikram Sambat dates use `DatePicker`.
`SymbolField` uppercases what is typed and matches by symbol and name through `searchSymbols`; it does not fetch.

Inside a Field as `SelectField`, or alone in a toolbar with a hidden label.
options with group to gather related choices under a heading.
avoid: Two to five short options that should all be visible: use `SegmentedControl` or `ChoiceGroup`.
Searching a long list by typing: use `SymbolField` or `CompanySearch`.

keyboard: `ArrowDown` and `ArrowUp` move through the results (wrapping). `ArrowLeft` and `ArrowRight` move between an entity row's action chips, wherever the caret is.
Enter runs the chosen action (the first unless moved). Tab moves between the field and the Esc button and never leaves the dialog. Esc closes it and focus goes back where it was.
A pointer resting on the list does not take the row back while you arrow.
accessibility: A modal dialog named by labels.dialog with a combobox field and a listbox; the active row is `aria-selected`.
Each entity row names its actions with `aria-describedby`, and a move between chips is announced in a polite status region (labels.chosen).
The hint bar at the foot is decorative; every label is a prop so the dialog can be fully translated.
The page does not scroll behind it.
responsive: On a phone it fills the screen.

items.title: Toast
items.description: What just happened: saved, failed or info messages in a polite live region, with an optional undo, wrapped once in ToastProvider and raised with useToast.
items.summary: A short message for what just happened: saved, failed, or a note, with an optional action such as Undo. Wrap the app once in ToastProvider and call useToast().show anywhere below it. At most three are visible, newest first, and each leaves by itself.
use: Confirming an action that has no other visible result: saved, removed, copied.
An undo for a removal: the action runs when pressed.
Errors the person can do nothing about on the spot (the form field keeps its own inline error).
avoid: Anything the person must read or answer: toasts disappear after 4 seconds (6 with an action).
The only place a validation error appears.
Many at once: only three show.

exports.name: ToastProvider
exports.description: Provides useToast to everything below it and renders the polite live region that holds the toasts (three at most; the stack itself is not live, two hidden regions announce each toast once, errors assertively, and hover or focus pauses its countdown).

props.name: children
props.description: The app (or the part of it) that may raise toasts with useToast. Render the provider once, near the root.

examples.title: Kinds and undo
examples.note: Success, error, info, and a toast with an Undo action.

keyboard: A toast's action button is a normal button in the tab order while it is shown. There is no key to dismiss one; it leaves on its own.
accessibility: The region is `aria-live="polite"`. An error toast has `role="alert"`; success and info are `role="status"`.
The title is bold and the body follows it; icons are decorative and the kind is also in the words.
Because toasts vanish, never put information only there that the person needs later.
responsive: Toasts stack in a fixed region at the edge of the viewport.

notes.title: Limits
points: `useToast` throws if it is used outside `ToastProvider`.
The display time and the three-toast cap are fixed (4 s, 6 s with an action; three). Words such as "Undo" are yours, so pass them in the reader's language.

items.title: Tooltip and InfoTip
items.description: A control's name on hover and focus, and a visible info button that explains a label. Neither holds the only copy of a fact, because a phone has no hover.
items.summary: Tooltip names a control that has only an icon; InfoTip explains a label on a visible ⓘ button beside it. Hover or keyboard focus shows either at once; an InfoTip click or tap keeps it open until Esc, a second tap, a tap elsewhere or a scroll. Never a native title attribute.
use: Tooltip on an icon-only button, to show its name.
`InfoTip` beside a term that needs a definition: cost basis, circuit limit.
trigger for a short text trigger instead of the icon.
avoid: Hiding the only copy of a fact in a hover tip: a phone has no hover.
Long content: an `InfoTip` is one or two sentences.
A native title attribute: it waits a second, never shows on a phone and gives no sign it is there.

props.name: content
props.description: The short text shown in the bubble: the control's name.

props.name: children
props.description: The one control the tooltip is for (a single element that can take aria-describedby).

props.name: describe
props.description: Also expose the text to screen readers as the control's description while shown, for a control that already has a visible name.

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the bubble.

props.name: label
props.description: What the button explains ("About weighted average cost"): its accessible name.

props.name: children
props.description: The explanation: one or two sentences. It is the button's description while shown.

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the button; the bubble is `${testId}-tip`.

props.name: trigger
props.description: A short text trigger instead of the default info icon.

examples.title: InfoTip
examples.note: An info button beside a label, and a text trigger.

keyboard: Tooltip shows at once on keyboard focus (focus-visible) and after 300 ms on mouse hover; Esc, blur, a press or leaving hides it.
`InfoTip` shows on focus or hover; Enter or Space pins it open; Esc, a second press, a press elsewhere or a scroll closes it.
accessibility: `InfoTip` is a button named by label; while shown, the text is its description (`aria-describedby`) in a `role="tooltip"` bubble.
A Tooltip repeats the control's own name, so it is hidden from screen readers (the name already says it). With describe it is exposed and the control gets `aria-describedby` while the tip is open.
The bubble is kept inside the window and placed so it does not cover the figure below a label. Clicks inside an `InfoTip` never open a clickable row it sits in.
responsive: On touch the `InfoTip` opens on tap and stays until dismissed. A Tooltip appears on hover and focus only, so keep its text redundant.

items.title: StatusPill
items.description: A short label for a state, a tone or a tag such as Bonus or New, with a marker form beside a title, and a CountBadge for how many are waiting.
items.summary: A short label: a state, a tone, a tag ("Bonus", "Estimate", "Yours", "New"). It is not pressable, except as a link with href. swatch adds a series colour square, size="sm" is the 20px tag, and marker is an outlined pill with a state dot for beside a page title (live, warn, off). CountBadge shows how many are waiting.
use: A status or tag in a row, a card header or beside a title.
marker for a market or data state next to a heading.
`CountBadge` beside a heading for a number of things waiting.
avoid: Something that looks pressable but is not: pills are labels.
Colour alone: the words must say the state.
A long sentence: keep to one or two words.

props.name: tone

props.name: dot

props.name: size

props.name: linkComponent

props.name: marker
props.description: A state beside a page's title (a market open, closed, delayed): an outlined pill whose dot carries the state; the words say it too.

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the pill.

props.name: className
props.description: Layout only (spacing in a row); never restyle the pill per page.

props.name: count
props.description: The number waiting.

props.name: label

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the badge.

examples.note: Six tones plus neutral, a dot, a small tag and a series swatch.

examples.title: Markers, link and count
examples.note: State markers, a pill as a link, and a CountBadge.

keyboard: A pill is not focusable unless it is a link (href); then it is a normal link: Tab, then Enter.
accessibility: The state is in the words; tone and dot are extra. A swatch is decorative (`aria-hidden`).
`CountBadge` is `role="img"` with `aria-label` (label), e.g. "2 waiting"; the heading beside it says what is counted.
responsive: Pills are inline and do not shrink below their text; let the row wrap.

items.title: LockedNote
items.description: The locked state of a data view: a lock and a plain line saying what is not included on this account. Never a plan name, never a blurred fake of the data.
items.summary: The locked state of a data view: a small lock and what is not included on this account. Give it one line, or a bold first line (title) and a second line under it. Say what is missing and, if you can, how to get it.
use: A panel whose data this account cannot see: broker activity, depth, an export.
Replacing a data view entirely, in the space the data would take.
avoid: Naming a plan or tier as the message.
Blurring or faking the data behind it.
An error: use an error state with a retry.

props.name: children
props.description: What is not included and, if you can say it, how to get it. With a `title` it is the line under it.

props.name: title
props.description: A bold first line ("Not included on this account"); the children are then the line under it.

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the note.

examples.title: With and without a title

keyboard: Not interactive. A link or button you place inside is.
accessibility: A paragraph (or a titled block) of text: the lock icon is decorative and the words say what is not included.
It is not a live region; if it appears after an action, announce that action separately.
responsive: Fills its container and wraps its text.
items.enforcementNote: UI is not enforcement. This component is a UX safeguard. It does not enforce anything. Authorisation, step-up authentication, limits, payee checks, session expiry and validation must be enforced on the server. Hidden or disabled controls are not access control.

items.title: Figure and Delta
items.description: Every number on a page: tabular digits with lakh and crore grouping, never truncated, and a change shown as a sign, an arrow, a colour and a spoken word.
items.summary: Figure prints a number with tabular digits and en-IN grouping, and is never truncated (it has its own element and no wrapping). Delta prints a change as a sign, an arrow, a colour and a spoken word, so colour never carries it alone. A move that prints as zero is no move: grey, no arrow. Missing values print a dash, never zero.
use: Any number you format for display in a row, a card or a sentence: a price, a count, a percent.
Delta for a day's change; words to translate "up", "down" and "unchanged".
avoid: Exact money: use `MoneyDisplay`, which takes bigint minor units and a currency.
`toFixed` on a price: it does not group and can round differently from the table.
Colour alone for gain and loss.

props.name: value
props.description:
The number to print. null, undefined and NaN print a dash, never zero.
Pass a `Money` (from `money(minor, currency)`) for an exact, currency-aware amount: it is printed by
`formatter`, or by Intl `en` for its currency, and `kind` and `dp` are ignored.

props.description: How to print a number: int (whole), pct (percent) or num (plain, default).

props.name: formatter
props.description: Money mode only: the formatter that prints a `Money` value (its currency must match). Default: Intl `en` for the currency.

props.name: dp
props.description: Decimals to print (default 2).

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the figure.

props.name: value
props.description: The change to print, signed. null, undefined and NaN print a dash. A value that rounds to zero at `dp` is neutral. A `Money` value prints exactly through `formatter` (`kind` and `dp` are ignored; zero is neutral).

props.name: kind
props.description: pct (default): 1.25%. num: a plain number.

props.name: formatter
props.description: Money mode only: the formatter that prints the amount. Default: Intl `en` for the currency.

props.name: dp
props.description: Decimals to print (default 2).

props.name: arrow
props.description: Show the up or down arrow (default true). Sign, colour and the spoken word remain.

props.name: size

props.description: Becomes data-testid on the figure.

keyboard: Figures are text and not interactive.
accessibility: Delta appends a visually hidden word (up, down, unchanged) after the number; arrows are `aria-hidden`. Pass words in the reader's language.
A figure that prints as 0.00 is neutral: it is grey and says "unchanged".
Figures use tabular numerals so columns align.
responsive: Figures do not wrap or truncate; give them room or let the table scroll.

notes.title: Limits
points: Figure and Delta take a JavaScript number and are for display only. Exact amounts, rounding and currency belong to `MoneyDisplay` and the calculations module.

items.title: LiveFigure
items.description: A figure fed by a live price: it counts to the new value over 450 ms and tints once in the direction of the change, and honours reduced motion.
items.summary: A plain figure that moves. When the value changes it counts to the new one over 450 ms (the same formatting at every frame, exactly the new value at the end) and its ground flashes the gain or loss tint for 900 ms. Under reduced motion it simply shows the new value. Live does the same for any figure through a render function.
use: A last traded price, a value or a weight that updates while it is on screen.
Live to move a Delta, a signed amount or a figure inside a sentence.
id to say what the figure stands for, so picking another row snaps instead of tweening.
avoid: Fetching inside it or around it: pass the value as a prop. See the Live data adapters guide.
Static numbers: use Figure.
`aria-live` on every cell: put it on one container that needs it.

props.name: value
props.description: The current value, from props or state. A change counts to it and tints once.

props.name: kind
props.description: How to print it: rs, int, pct or num (default), as in Figure.

props.name: dp
props.description: Decimals to print (default 2).

props.name: id
props.description: What the figure stands for (a symbol); a new id snaps instead of moving.

props.description: Extra classes on the wrapper, for layout.

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the wrapper.

props.name: value
props.description: The current value, from props or state. A change moves the figure to it.

props.name: id
props.description: What the figure stands for; a new id snaps (picking another row is not a price move).

props.name: dp
props.description: Decimals the figure prints (a smaller change is no move).

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the wrapper, for layout.

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the wrapper. Put it here, never inside `children`.

props.name: children
props.description: Draws the figure for the value n it is given (the in-between values while it moves, then exactly `value`).

examples.title: A live price
examples.note: Tick up and down to see the count and the tint; switching the id snaps.

examples.title: Any figure
examples.note: Live with a render function moves a Delta.

keyboard: Not interactive.
accessibility: While it moves, the frames are hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`) and the final value is read from a visually hidden copy; at rest there is one element.
Put `aria-live` on a container that needs it (the open stock's price), never on every cell.
The tint is extra: the value itself changes. Reduced motion turns off both the count and the tint.
responsive: Same as Figure: it never wraps or truncates.

notes.title: Limits
points: Put a test id on Live itself, never inside children: the final value is drawn twice while it moves.
A change below the printed precision (dp decimals) is no move: no tween and no tint.

items.title: Page layout and header
items.description: The page ground, the page header with a back circle, a large title, a meta line and up to three actions, and the section header: a title with one action.

use: `PageHeader` at the top of every page, with the one h1.
`ListSectionHeader` over a group of rows or a card.
stamp to say what the page's figures are as of; eyebrow for the page's group.
avoid: More than one `PageHeader` or `PageLayout` per page.
More than three actions in the header.
A back link on a root page: omit `backTo`.

Your own navigation component passed as `navigation`.

Using it inside a layout that already provides a main element.

current for a jump link in an in-page section nav.

A yes/no filter: the label alone with its x.
Showing that a filter cannot apply (error) while the editor says why.
avoid: A plain toggle with no value: use Chip.
A filter that has no editor and no removal: that is a `StatusPill`.
Colour alone for the error ring: say why in the editor.

exports.name: FilterChip
exports.description:

set, in words ("P/B 0.00 to 1.20"). The chip opens its editor; its ×
removes it. A chip with a caret and no × opens a list (Sector · All). It is
a 36px box like the other controls in a bar; each of its two buttons draws
its own single focus ring. A filter with nothing to edit (a yes/no filter)
is the label alone with its ×.

The x has its own accessible name from `removeLabel` ("Remove P/B"); it is required with `onRemove`.
The error ring is extra: the editor must say what is wrong in words.
responsive: A 36px box that wraps with its neighbours; the x keeps a 44px tap area on touch.

keyboard: Not interactive. Tab order is the order of the children in the document, so the visual order should match it.
accessibility: They add no role. With `as="ul"` or `as="ol"` the children must be `li`; `as="nav"` and `as="section"` need an `aria-label`.

items.title: CodeBlock

items.summary: A block of plain text in a monospace box, for output a person reads or copies: a CSV export, a JSON payload, an account statement. The text is shown exactly as given. Add a `label` to name it, and `copy` for a Copy button that puts the whole text on the clipboard. It does not colour syntax.
use: Showing the CSV a user is about to download.
A JSON response or a reference number to copy (`copy`).
avoid: Long source code: it is plain text, with no highlighting or line numbers.
A secret such as a full account number: the copy button puts it on a clipboard shared with every app.
Columns of figures: use a table.

items.title: Chart scales
items.description: Pure Y scales for value charts: round ticks that bracket the line so it fills the plot, and a far-off second series named instead of squashed at the edge.
items.summary: Two pure functions for value charts. bracketScale picks round ticks (1, 2, 2.5, 3, 4 or 5 of a power of ten) so the lowest tick is at or below the data and the highest at or above, and the line fills the plot. valueScale brackets the value line alone and reports whether a second series such as the money invested lies below or above it.
use: A portfolio value line with a benchmark or an amount invested.
Your own SVG chart that should look like the kit's.
avoid: Candles and volumes: use chart-math (`niceTicks`).
Rendering: these return numbers and a y function only.

exports.name: bracketScale
exports.description:
A Y scale whose round ticks bracket the data: the lowest tick at or below
the smallest value, the highest at or above the largest, and the domain is
exactly that tick range, so the top tick is labelled and the line fills the
plot. The data gets a 4% margin first (the line never sits on the edge),
then the step (1, 2, 2.5, 3, 4 or 5 of a power of ten) that gives 3 to 6
ticks with the least empty space wins.
exports.signature: (min: number, max: number, f: ScaleFrame) => BracketScale

exports.name: valueScale
exports.description:
The value-led scale: bracketed on `values` alone. A `second` series wholly
below or above that range is left off (`off` says which side); one that is
partly inside is taken into the range, so it is drawn whole.
exports.signature: (values: readonly number[], second: readonly number[], f: ScaleFrame) => { scale: BracketScale; off: OffRange; }

examples.title: A value line
examples.note: Five weekly values with one missing; the invested series is off the plot.

keyboard: Not a UI module.
accessibility: Nothing to render. When off is below or above, name that series in your legend so it is not lost.
responsive: Not applicable.

notes.title: Guarantees
points: The domain is exactly the tick range, so the top tick is labelled and the line never sits on the plot edge (a 4% margin first).
A flat series (min equals max) still gets a range of 3 to 6 ticks.
A second series partly inside the range is taken into it, so it is drawn whole; only a series wholly outside it is left off.

items.summary: Two panes side by side (or one above the other) and a separator between them. The separator is a WAI-ARIA window splitter: it takes focus, reports the start pane's share as its value, moves with the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps), Home and End, and Enter collapses the start pane to its minimum and restores it. Dragging uses pointer capture, so it works with a mouse, a pen and a finger. The share is a percent of the container; below 640 px of container width the panes stack and the separator is hidden.
use: A chart and an order ticket, a list and its detail, a table and a preview.
Controlled `size` with `onSizeChange` to remember the split (for example with `useLocalStorage`).
avoid: Fixed sidebars that people never resize: a CSS grid is simpler.
Nesting many split panes: two levels at most stay understandable.

items.title: PercentageInput
items.description: A field for rates such as brokerage, commission and interest. The value is an exact decimal string, never a float, with Devanagari digits and min and max.
items.summary: A field for a rate: brokerage, commission, interest, a discount. The value is a plain decimal string in percent units ('0.4' means 0.4%), never a float. Devanagari and Arabic-Indic digits and a pasted percent sign are accepted, a fraction longer than `maxFractionDigits` is refused rather than rounded, and `onValueChange` reports the exact string, a state, the rate in basis points as a bigint and whether it is outside `min` and `max`.
use: A fee, commission, interest or tax rate the person types: brokerage on a trade, the rate on a fixed deposit, a loan margin.
Multiply an amount by `basisPoints` with `divideRounded` from `@punji/ui/calculations` and a rounding mode you choose; the field never rounds for you.
`min` and `max` for the range your product allows (for example 0 to 100). The message appears once the field is left; pass `error` to say it your way.
avoid: Money: use `CurrencyInput`. Counts and lots: use `NumberField`.
Reading the display text (`digits="deva"` shows Devanagari): read `onValueChange`.
Treating `min` and `max` as validation on their own. They guide the person; check the rate again on your server.

keyboard: Standard text input: type, paste, Tab in and out.
A paste is cleaned (spaces and a percent sign dropped, Devanagari digits converted) and refused whole when it is not a rate.
On blur, an unfinished "12." becomes "12" and a lone "-" or "." clears.
accessibility: A native `<label for>`; "(percent)" is added to the accessible name, and the visible % is hidden from screen readers.
Hint and error use `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`; the error is a live `role="alert"`.
`inputMode="decimal"` asks a phone for the decimal keypad. The text is right-aligned so digits line up in a column of rates.
responsive: Fills its container; `size="lg"` gives a 44px target for forms and `md` suits a toolbar.

notes.title: Limits
points: `basisPoints` is exact only up to two fraction digits (0.01%). With `maxFractionDigits` above 2 it is null when the rate needs more; use `value` and your own exact arithmetic then.
Out-of-range values are reported, not clamped, so what was typed stays visible. `state` is 'partial' for text such as "12." or "-".
Only a dot is accepted as the decimal mark, because Nepali and Indian locales use it and a comma could be a group mark.

items.title: OtpInput
items.description: A one-time code field with one box per character: paste and SMS autofill, numeric or alphanumeric, masked option, one group label, and left-to-right in RTL.
items.summary: A one-time code as one box per character. The group has one label and each box has its own name ("Digit 3 of 6"). Typing moves forward, Backspace moves back, the arrows, Home and End move between boxes, and a paste or an SMS autofill spreads across the boxes. Numeric by default, alphanumeric on request, with an option to mask the characters. The boxes always run left to right, even on a right-to-left page.
use: Confirming a bank or broker transaction, login or password reset with a code sent by SMS or an authenticator app.
`onComplete` to submit as soon as the last box is filled; `value` and `onChange` when you hold the code in state.
`mask` for a PIN. `name` to submit the code with a form.
avoid: Checking the code in the browser: the code is verified on your server, and the field never knows whether it is right.
Long free-form codes: use a normal `Field`. Boxes suit 4 to 8 characters (the limit is 12).

props.name: hint

props.description: Disable every box.

props.description: Focus the first empty box on mount.

props.name: id
props.description: Id prefix; generated when omitted.

props.name: testId
props.description: Becomes data-testid on the group.

props.name: size
props.description: Box size: 'lg' (44, default) or 'md' (36).

props.name: cellLabel
props.description: The accessible name of one box. Default "Digit 3 of 6" (or "Character" when alphanumeric).

examples.title: Masked PIN
examples.note: mask turns the boxes into password boxes; paste and keyboard work the same.

examples.title: Error and alphanumeric
examples.note: A rejected code marks every box invalid and is announced; an eight-character recovery code accepts letters too.

keyboard: Typing a character fills the box and moves to the next. Focus cannot skip an empty box: clicking ahead moves to the first empty one.
Backspace clears the current box (or the previous one when the current is empty) and moves back; Delete clears the current box.
ArrowLeft and ArrowRight, Home and End move between boxes. Paste fills from the box where it lands; a full-length code replaces everything.
accessibility: One `role="group"` named by the visible label, linked to the hint or error with `aria-describedby`; each box is named separately ("Digit 3 of 6"), translatable through `cellLabel`.
The first box has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so iOS and Android offer the SMS code and the whole code arrives in one change, which the field spreads across the boxes.
The boxes are `dir="ltr"` always, because a code is read in the order it was sent; the label, hint and error follow the page direction. Boxes are 44px (`md` is 36px).
An error is a `role="alert"` and sets `aria-invalid` on every box.
responsive: Boxes shrink to fit a narrow container; at 8 or more boxes on a phone they drop below 44px, so keep codes to six where you can.

notes.title: Limits
points: Not reviewed with VoiceOver or NVDA yet (see the roadmap).
Devanagari and Arabic-Indic digits are converted to ASCII; other scripts are dropped.

items.enforcementNote: UI is not enforcement. This component is a UX safeguard. It does not enforce anything. Authorisation, step-up authentication, limits, payee checks, session expiry and validation must be enforced on the server. Hidden or disabled controls are not access control.

items.title: StatementUpload

Accepted files are listed with name and size and can be removed. It makes no network request: you receive the files in `onChange` and upload them yourself.

`accept` and `maxSize` to set the rules; `multiple` and `maxFiles` for several months at once.
`onReject` to log or show refusals your own way; `error` for a failed upload.

Uploading from inside the component: it deliberately has no URL, and holds no credentials.
Sensitive statements over a page you do not serve over HTTPS.

keyboard: Tab to "Choose file" and press Enter or Space to open the file picker; this is the full keyboard route, dragging is an extra for pointer users.
Each file has a Remove button; after removing, focus returns to "Choose file".
accessibility: A `role="group"` named by the visible label and described by the hint and any errors.

notes.title: Security boundary
points: The component reads only the file name, size and type, never the contents. A file named .csv can hold anything; check the content on the server.
Statements are sensitive. Send them over HTTPS to your own server and do not keep them in the browser longer than the upload.
For CSV imports of amounts, parse them with `parseMinorUnits` so a value is never rounded silently.

items.title: Date range presets
items.description: Quick ranges for DateRangePicker: Today, This week, This month, Last 30 days and the Nepal fiscal year (Shrawan to Asar) to date, as pure exact functions.
items.summary: Pure helpers that turn today's date into the ranges people pick most, and a `presets` prop on `DateRangePicker` that shows them as buttons above the calendar. The Nepal fiscal year runs from 1 Shrawan to the end of Asar and is computed from Bikram Sambat tables; a Gregorian fiscal year takes its start month. Everything is a civil date string (YYYY-MM-DD) and never reads the clock or the time zone.
use: Statement, report and history filters where "this month" and "fiscal year to date" are the common choices.
`nepalDateRangePresets` for Nepal: BS months and the Shrawan fiscal year. `dateRangePresets` with `fiscalYearStartMonth` for another country (4 for April, 7 for July).
Pass `today` from your own clock in the business time zone (`instantToNepalDate`); the helpers never read the clock.
avoid: Calling `new Date()` inside the helpers' callers without choosing a time zone: near midnight the day will differ from Kathmandu.
Expecting a future end date. This week, This month and Year to date end today because the future has no entries.

notes.title: Limits

A preset applies immediately and does not move the open calendar; if you want the person to adjust it first, let them pick days in the calendar instead.

items.title: App header
items.description: A trading account’s top bar built from Punji UI: section links, company search, the NEPSE market mark, inbox and avatar, with the index strip.
items.summary: The bar every signed-in screen starts with. The brand and the section links sit on the left, company search in the middle and the market mark, the inbox and the account on the right; under it the index strip and the page’s title row with its freshness note and actions. items.description: Exact NEPSE trade costs in paisa: broker commission bands, SEBON fee, DP charge and capital gains tax by holding period, all configurable.
items.summary: Pure TypeScript for the cost of a NEPSE trade: no React, no browser, no dependency. Amounts are bigint paisa and every rate is a decimal string, so nothing is a float. `estimateNepseTrade` returns the amount, broker commission, SEBON fee, DP charge, capital gains tax on a sell, the total payable or receivable, and the effective price per unit. Every figure comes from a `NepseFeeSchedule`; `nepseFeeSchedule` is a dated example to verify, not an authority.

avoid: Treating the estimate as the contract note. The broker's note is final; show the estimate as an estimate.
Floats anywhere: convert typed text with `parseMinorUnits`, never `Number`.
Hard-coding today's rates in your app: keep one schedule object, dated, and replace it.

items.title: Share issue helpers
items.description: Pure helpers: issue status, kitta rules, BOID checks, bonus and right entitlements, adjusted price after book close and WACC, exact in bigint.
items.summary: Pure functions behind `@punji/ui/share-issues`, with no React, no browser globals and no calendar converter. Issues: `issueStatus`, `sortIssues`, `checkKitta`, `parseKitta`, `nearestValidKitta`, `issueAmount`. BOIDs: `checkBoid`, `boidParts`, `formatBoid`, `spokenBoid`. Corporate actions: `entitledUnits` (bonus or right, fractional units dropped by default), `adjustedPrice` ((price + right% × right price) / (1 + bonus% + right%), one final rounding), `costBasisSteps` and `costBasisAfter` for WACC through buys, bonus, right and sales (average cost), and `corporateTimeline`. Money is bigint paisa; percentages are decimal strings; every rounding is a RoundingMode you choose.
use: The same rules on the server (Node) as in the browser.
A WACC table for capital-gains estimates: `unitCost` on a bonus prices bonus units the way your tax rule does.
avoid: Floats anywhere: pass bigint paisa and percent strings.
Treating `adjustedPrice` as the exchange's published figure: use it to explain the jump, compare with the official price.
